6b401f739d69dfcd: JOHOR BARU: A company administrator was duped into transferring RM110,000 after a caller posing as her director instructed her to make several payments.
Police are also investigating whether the suspect mimicked the actual director's voice using deepfake technology.
The 43-year-old woman, who works for a construction company, received a call from a man who introduced himself as 'Lei Chong' and 'director Lei', claiming to be her employer.

Johor Baru (South) police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said the caller instructed the woman to go to an office in Larkin before directing her to make several payments into two bank accounts.
"The total amount transferred was RM110,000 using company funds," he said in a statement today.
The caller then demanded another RM150,000 be transferred to a different bank account.
The woman, who had grown suspicious, contacted the actual company director via WeChat and discovered that he had never instructed her to make any payments.
Azrul Hisham said investigations were underway to identify the bank account holders, verify the transactions with the respective banks and trace the suspects.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating, which carries a jail term of up to 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.

He urged the public, particularly those handling company finances, to verify payment instructions directly with the purported sender, even when the caller appears to be a known employer, company director or government officer.
Those who suspect they have fallen victim to a scam should contact the National Scam Response Centre at 997 immediately.

3099ffb23eef7651: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's manufacturing sector recorded a 9.1 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in sales value to RM177.3 billion in July 2026, driven mainly by the electrical and electronics (E&E) products sub-sector.

However, the sector's sales value edged up 0.2 per cent month-on-month (MoM), according to the Statistics Department in a statement on Wednesday, Sept 9. It was also a lower rate of growth compared with the 9.8 per cent rate in June.

During the month, sales of E&E products led the sector's growth, registering 17.8 per cent YoY, while the food, beverages and tobacco sub-sector expanded 3.9 per cent, accelerating from 2.2 per cent in June.
The petroleum, chemical, rubber and plastic sub-sector recorded growth of 3.6 per cent.

The export-oriented industry led the manufacturing sector sales value growth in July, recording a 9.9 per cent increase from a year ago, while domestic industries' growth moderated to 7.2 per cent YoY.
Export-oriented manufacturing sales contributed 72.2 per cent to the total value in July.
The department said the growth was anchored by the manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products, which increased 19 per cent, followed by machinery and equipment at 17.8 per cent YoY.
The manufacture of coke and refined petroleum products also expanded 3.3 per cent.
However, on a MoM basis, July sales value of export-oriented industries declined 1.0 per cent, according to the Statistics Department.
Domestic-oriented industry's sales value growth was led by the manufacture of basic metals, which grew 14.9 per cent YoY, up from 10.6 per cent in June

This was followed by the manufacture of food processing products, which grew 9.6 per cent from seven per cent previously, while the manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers rose five per cent.
From the previous month, sales value of domestic-oriented industries increased 3.2 per cent, the department stated.

For the first seven months of 2026, cumulative manufacturing sales value reached RM1.20 trillion, up 7.6 per cent from the same period last year, compared with a 3.7 per cent increase in January-July 2025.
*MANUFACTURING EMPLOYMENT INCREASE IN JULY*

On the employment side, the Statistics Department stated that the number of employees in the manufacturing sector rose 1.1 per cent YoY to 2.4 million in July, supported by the food, beverages and tobacco sub-sector, which grew 2.2 per cent.

This was followed by the non-metallic mineral products, basic metal and fabricated metal products sub-sector, which grew 1.9 per cent YoY, compared with 1.6 per cent in June, and the E&E products sub-sector at 1.3 per cent.
On a monthly basis, manufacturing employment increased 0.1 per cent, reversing a 0.2 per cent decline in June.
Salaries and wages paid in the sector increased 2.8 per cent YoY to RM8.55 billion in July, although this was 0.5 per cent lower than in June.
Sales value per employee rose 7.9 per cent YoY to RM73,188, while average salaries and wages per employee increased 1.7 per cent to RM3,527.
During the first seven months of the year, manufacturing employment increased 1.1 per cent YoY to 2.4 million, while salaries and wages paid rose 2.7 per cent to RM60.1 billion.
Sales value per employee also increased 6.4 per cent to RM496,792, according to the Statistics Department.

ef455df582384d7d: LOS ANGELES: Pounding surf lashing the swanky California enclave of Malibu on Tuesday opened up a giant sinkhole on the driveway of a house reportedly belonging to US actor Nicolas Cage.
Aerial pictures taken by AFP show concrete and other detritus have slid into the hole on the road side of the multi-million-dollar oceanfront property.
Traffic cones are set back from the crater, which appears to be perilously close to swallowing the house's double garage.

Waves that are pounding the sea front can be seen lapping in the hole, and rushing out again under the stanchions that support the home, which entertainment outlet TMZ said belonged to the "Leaving Las Vegas" star.
Richard Thompson, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, told AFP coastal waters off Southern California were being roiled by the remnants of Hurricane Marie.
"There were some pretty significant surf and swells across area in the last several days," he said.
"At the height of the surf and swell, we had some very significant wave heights up 3-4.5 metres in some spots, along with significant beach erosion."
The high surf in California comes as another storm system, Hurricane Lowell, lashed Hawaii with damaging winds, heavy rainfall and powerful floods, blacking out power across most of one island.
A near-record-strength El Nino climate episode is warming the waters of the Pacific Ocean and promoting the formation of powerful storms.
While the warming phase is a natural phenomenon, scientists believe the human-caused heating of the climate could make its effects much larger.
3b4d847363845567: WASHINGTON, Sept 9 — In President Donald Trump’s telling at a White House event yesterday, two firefighters bodily lifted him to safety from a site near an unstable building after the September 11, 2001 attacks.

“And I’ll never forget,” Trump said, “we thought it was coming down on top of us, and two firemen, big strong guys — and I’m not the smallest guy in the world — they grabbed me under the arm, said, ‘Got to get out of here!’” Trump said.

His comments, at an event honouring emergency personnel killed on 9/11, appeared to be a new instalment in a constantly evolving narrative that Trump has told over the years about his actions after the attacks.
It’s a story that has long featured the New York property tycoon as the hero, with variations on him taking workers down to Ground Zero.
But Trump’s version of events is one that US media say is disputed by rescue officials present at the time.
The remarks also come amid a stir about Trump not being present as president in New York for the 25th anniversary of the attacks in which 2,977 people were killed.

Instead of being at the site where Al-Qaeda hijackers rammed planes into the World Trade Centre towers, Trump will pay his respects on Friday at the Pentagon in Washington, another target in the attacks.
Trump and the White House have hotly denied reports that he chose the Pentagon because he was not allowed to deliver a speech at the 9/11 memorial.
“This is more Corrupt News, I’ve been to New York many times over the years, and no one ever speaks, it’s a ‘solemn ceremony!’” Trump said on his Truth Social network last week.
But it will still place the 80-year-old native New Yorker away from the main focus of the day’s commemorative events.

Vice President JD Vance and Trump’s four living predecessors—Democrats Joe Biden, Barack Obama and Bill Clinton, as well as Republican George W Bush, who was president at the time of the attacks—are all expected at “Ground Zero.”
Later on Friday, Trump is due to fly to Ireland where he will attend the Irish Open golf tournament at his family’s golf course over the weekend.
‘More famous than me’
His absence from New York marks a contrast with Trump’s usual approach, which has been to put himself at the heart of the 9/11 story.

Two days after the attacks, Trump told reporters that he had been to Ground Zero and had sent 100 workers to the site to help recovery efforts. CNN and the New York Times said people present at the site disputed his account.
In the event on the White House Ellipse yesterday, where a steel beam recovered from the World Trade Centre’s South Tower was on display, Trump gave a fresh account of his actions that day.
Trump said it had been a “beautiful morning” and that he had then seen a news alert on television, before looking out of his window “and I saw things that I never want to see again.”
He added that he was overseeing a building project and that he “took the whole crew down there right after this happened.”
Trump clarified his recollections in a lengthy Truth Social Post yesterday evening.

“I was there, obviously not on the same day as the collapse, but shortly thereafter, with a large group of Construction Workers,” Trump wrote, in a post accompanied by a video showing answering reporters’ questions.
“I was there as soon as the Law allowed,” the US president added, as he lashed out at journalists and accused them of spreading “fake news.”
At yesterday’s event, Trump meanwhile presented the highest US civilian honour to the family of volunteer firefighter Welles Crowther, who was killed while helping lead people out of the South Tower.
Crowther, an equities trader, became known as the “man in the red bandana” after survivors told stories about a mysterious man wearing one over his nose and mouth.
“The Man in the Red Bandana. He’s become more famous than me, I don’t like it,” Trump said with a chuckle. — AFP

60da2a0317e5571a: KUALA LUMPUR: Azeem Fahmi believes the 4x100m relay team can create a surprise at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, which begin on Sept 19, by finishing on the podium.
Azeem anchored the 4x100m quartet of Pengiran Aidil Auf Hajam, Danish Iftikhar Roslee and Umaira Subri to clock 39.18 seconds to win gold in the Oman Grand Prix in Muscat on Sept 5.
The quartet was just a whisker away from the national 4x100m record of 39.03 set at the 2025 Thailand SEA Games last December.
Malaysia's B 4x100m quartet of Umar Osman, Armin Zahryl Abdul Latif, Sayyid Amin Roslan and Haziq Akhir posted 41.29 to bag bronze.
"It is very interesting that there are many young sprinters in the country with a lot of potential, like Danish Iftikhar, who is very consistent in competitions.
"We are leading a new generation of sprinters and also the formation of a new 4x100m relay team. I am excited to lead them as team captain for the 4x100m for the Asian Games.
"I, with no hesitation, believe in the ability of the sprinters that the relay team can create a surprise in the Asian Games.
"Although there are other strong 4x100m teams from China, Japan, and South Korea on paper, they can fumble in the event on race day.
"Malaysia will start as underdogs but we want to execute the race well and hopefully things will fall well into the right place at the right time," said Azeem.
Azeem, who holds the national record of 10.09 in 100m, ran in the blue riband event in Muscat, where he clocked 10.37 in the heats.

"There are many good sprinters in Asia whom I can level with as seniors and more experienced, and some of them have achieved way more in their track and field career," said Azeem, who clocked 10.11 to win bronze in the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games.
"As for me, I consider myself a young sprinter, as I am 22 years old, still a long way to go for me. For this edition of the games, I am going to the Asian Games with the mindset of doing my best.
"I want to pick up where I left off before. Everyone knows that I won bronze, which no one expected me to do.
"For my second Asian Games, my goal is to qualify for the final first. If I can achieve that, then I believe that I can repeat the same thing or even do better."
ba0acaa94f450240: TOKYO, Sept 9 — Hundreds of Asian Games athletes in Japan were briefly evacuated from their accommodation as record rainfall lashed host city Nagoya, with competition beginning tomorrow.
Rainwater also leaked into some competition venues, with more wet weather forecast for the coming days.
About 104mm of rain fell in an hour in Nagoya yesterday, prompting municipal officials to issue an evacuation order for parts of the city.
Scientists say human-induced climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of weather events in Japan and elsewhere.
There is no dedicated athletes’ village at this year’s Asian Games, with organisers instead relying on a cruise ship, temporary wooden containers and hotels.

A view of India’s first container-based accommodation for sportspersons preparing to participate in the upcoming Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026, at Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports in Patiala September 3, 2026. There is no dedicated athletes’ village at this year’s Asian Games, with organisers instead relying on a cruise ship, temporary wooden containers and hotels. — AFP pic
An official with Nagoya Port Authority told AFP that “hundreds” of athletes staying at the city’s Garden Pier area, where the wooden container huts are located, were told to move to safety.
The athletes returned after the evacuation order was lifted about two hours later.
The Asian Games officially begin with an opening ceremony on September 19 but several events get under way before that.
Rainwater was found in several competition venues but Nagoya Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa said the facilities were not seriously affected and that events would go on as scheduled.
“There has been limited impact like rainwater leaking from the roofs of some buildings, but the situation is not so serious that the opening on the 19th is in jeopardy for now,” he said.
“Given the current circumstances, I believe there will be no obstacles to holding the Asian Games.”
More than 17,000 athletes and officials are expected at the Games — a bigger number than the Olympics.
Subway and bus services in Nagoya were temporarily halted on Tuesday and the Japan Meteorological Agency issued its highest flood warning for a major river in the area. — AFP

cdc4dfb650094979: TEMERLOH, Sept 9 — A former childcare assistant was charged at the Sessions Court here today with abusing a two-year-old boy at a childcare centre in Mentakab last month.
Nor Ain Ashikin Husin, 26, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read out before Judge Jamaludin Mat.
According to the charge, she allegedly abused the child in a manner that could have caused emotional injury at a childcare centre in Taman Keramat Indah, Mentakab, at about 9.45am on Aug 11.
She was charged under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both, upon conviction.
The prosecution offered bail of RM10,000 with one surety, but the defence sought a lower amount, citing that the accused was no longer employed and the surety could only provide RM5,000.

Previously, police confirmed receiving a report over the alleged assault after a video of the incident went viral on social media. — Bernama
2fde9054f57c3279: KUALA SELANGOR, Sept 9 — Police have crippled a drug processing and distribution syndicate and uncovered a drug laboratory in Puncak Alam here through Op Eumenes conducted in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, with the total drugs seized estimated to be worth RM2.4 billion on Aug 15.

Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said three local men and a foreign man and woman, aged between 29 and 43, were arrested in six separate raids conducted around Kuala Lumpur and Selangor.

“During the raids, we seized various types of drugs weighing an estimated 13.17 tonnes, including cannabis, Erimin 5, ketamine, yaba and methamphetamine, as well as various machines and equipment believed to have been used to process drugs at the premises in the industrial area,” he said at a press conference at an industrial area in Puncak Alam here today.
Elaborating, Hussein said the total value of the drugs seized was estimated at RM2.4 billion, making it the biggest drug seizure believed to have been recorded this year.

He said the syndicate, which is believed to have been active since February, used a modus operandi of obtaining drug supplies and processing equipment believed to have been brought in from China before being smuggled into Malaysia.
Police also found a container inside the drug laboratory premises which is believed to be linked to the syndicate’s modus operandi of bringing in materials and equipment from overseas.
Meanwhile, he said police believed the syndicate leader was an individual who was shot dead in a previous raid in Seremban.

He said the individual was believed to have managed the rental of the premises, the entry of precursor materials (chemical compounds) and equipment from overseas, as well as recruitment of syndicate members.

The media had previously reported that police crippled a drug processing syndicate believed to be producing methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) worth RM27.5 million through Op Thrips in Seremban and Kuala Lumpur on Sept 6.
Meanwhile, Hussein said one of the suspects, a Taiwanese, was believed to have acted as the syndicate’s chemist and had entered the country four times.
“We are still investigating the possibility that the syndicate has a network in Taiwan and will cooperate with the authorities there,” he said.

Several syndicate members had yet to be arrested, including one who was believed to have fled the country, while investigations were also underway to determine whether there was any possible involvement of insiders from other agencies.
“All the suspects were charged in court under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 on Aug 21 and 27.
Meanwhile, Hussein also revealed that the syndicate was believed to be linked to a kidnapping victim in Selangor in July.

On July 18, the media reported that police had rescued a man who was kidnapped within 48 hours and arrested six individuals, including a woman, who were believed to have demanded RM7 million in ransom in a special operation at a residential unit in the i-City area, Shah Alam, Selangor. — Bernama
bfafc93cd4df19b0: *Universiti Malaya researchers are investigating how climate processes in the Arctic and Antarctic may be connected to Malaysia’s monsoons and rainfall.
SEPTEMBER 9 — Malaysians may be thousands of kilometres from the Arctic and Antarctic, but changes at the poles may not be as distant from our daily lives as they seem.

Our weather is shaped by a climate system that extends far beyond Malaysia. The Northeast Monsoon brings periods of intense rainfall that can lead to major flooding, particularly along the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia. Understanding the wider climate processes associated with monsoon variability is therefore important as the global climate continues to change.

Scientists have long known that climate conditions in one part of the world can influence weather elsewhere. A familiar example is El Niño. Although it begins with changes in the tropical Pacific Ocean, El Niño conditions are commonly associated with hotter and drier conditions in Malaysia, while La Niña can contribute to wetter conditions.

Scientists call these long-distance climate relationships teleconnections. Researchers are increasingly examining how the tropics and polar regions are connected through large-scale atmospheric and oceanic processes. For Malaysia, this raises an important question: how might climate variability at high latitudes relate to the monsoon systems that influence our region?

Understanding tropical-polar connections has been part of Malaysia’s Antarctic research for more than two decades. Early work led by Emeritus Professor Datuk Dr Azizan Abu Samah at the National Antarctic Research Centre (NARC), Universiti Malaya, helped establish research into links between polar and tropical climate systems. Building on this foundation, NARC researchers continue to investigate these relationships and their relevance to monsoon variability.

Research involving the group has examined the relationship between Antarctic sea-ice extent in the Indian Ocean sector and the Indian Summer Monsoon. The findings contribute to a growing body of research on the atmospheric processes connecting Antarctic climate variability with lower latitudes.

The team is also interested in understanding climate processes associated with the Northeast Monsoon over Malaysia. One relevant large-scale pattern is the Arctic Oscillation (AO), which describes variations in atmospheric pressure between the Arctic and the mid-latitudes. The AO can influence atmospheric circulation over East Asia, including the Siberian High and the occurrence of cold surges.
The poles may be at the ends of the Earth, but understanding their connections with the tropics can help us better understand the climate closer to home. — Pexels pic

Cold surges are pulses of strong northeasterly winds that move across the South China Sea during the Northeast Monsoon. As these winds travel southwards, they can gain moisture over the sea and influence rainfall over Southeast Asia. Previous research involving Universiti Malaya researchers has shown that cold surges and their interaction with other regional weather systems can contribute to episodes of heavy rainfall over Peninsular Malaysia.

For Malaysia, understanding these processes can improve scientific knowledge of monsoon variability and the atmospheric conditions associated with extreme rainfall. However, the pathways linking polar climate variability, regional atmospheric circulation and Malaysian weather are complex and remain an active area of research.

Malaysia is also contributing to international efforts to advance understanding of tropical–polar climate connections. Associate Professor Dr Sheeba Chenoli of Universiti Malaya has chaired the Tropical Antarctic Teleconnections (TATE) Action Group, under the Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research (SCAR), since 2018.

The initiative brings together researchers from across disciplines and regions to investigate the complex interactions and teleconnections between the tropics and Antarctica, strengthening international collaboration and advancing knowledge of how changes in one region can influence climate variability and extremes in the other region.

During the XXXIX SCAR Delegates Meeting, held in Oslo, Norway, from August 17–19, 2026, following the 12th SCAR Open Science Conference, the TATE Action Group was formally transitioned into a SCAR Expert Group. This work forms part of Malaysia’s wider Antarctic research efforts through NARC and Yayasan Penyelidikan Antartika Sultan Mizan (Sultan Mizan Antarctic Research Foundation), strengthening the country’s contribution to international polar and climate science.

For a tropical country such as Malaysia, polar research may initially seem remote. Yet studying the Arctic and Antarctic also contributes to understanding a global climate system in which changes and variability in one region can be connected to processes far beyond it.
The poles may be at the ends of the Earth, but understanding their connections with the tropics can help us better understand the climate closer to home.
*The author is a meteorologist and climatologist who is Head of the Physical Science Group at the National Antarctic Research Centre, Universiti Malaya, and can be reached at sheeba@um.edu.my
** This is the personal opinion of the writers or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
9e5c0672831eabc2: JOHOR BARU: The magistrates' court here has set Sept 18 for a decision on the case involving two married couples accused of assaulting three Indonesian domestic helpers in December.

The date was fixed after the prosecution sought time to obtain further instructions from the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC), following the complainants' decision to settle the matter outside court.
Magistrate A. Shaarmini allowed the application by deputy public prosecutor Nurul Syafiqah Sha'ari.
The four accused — Muhamad Firdaus Sha'aban, 33, his wife Nurafiqah Nabila Hazhar, 33, Muhamad Hirzihaziq Abulae's, 30, and his wife Nurfarah Ainna Hazhar, 34 — were present in court today.
Their lawyer, Kamal Hisham Jaafar, said the three Indonesian domestic helpers had voluntarily withdrawn their police reports against his clients at several police stations yesterday.
He said his clients had also withdrawn their police reports linked to the case.
"The settlement was reached through the cooperation of all parties, including the Indonesian consulate-general in Johor.
"The matter has been resolved amicably and harmoniously," he told reporters outside the court.
Kamal said the settlement was important as the case had attracted widespread attention, particularly among the Indonesian community in Malaysia.
He said police would interview the complainants following the withdrawal of the reports to ensure the decision was made voluntarily and without coercion.
The four were charged at the same court on June 22, with Firdaus facing five charges while each of the other three accused faced three charges.
All four pleaded not guilty to the charges.
They were granted bail. Firdaus RM11,500, RM5,500 for Nurafiqah, and RM9,000 each for Hirzihaziq and Nurfarah Ainna.
The case came to light after a video went viral of one of the Indonesian women being assaulted for allegedly abusing the child of one of the couples.

d9ba022cc5b7c043: KUALA LUMPUR: Perkhidmatan doktor udara (FDS) akan diteruskan meskipun berlaku nahas helikopter di Ulu Baram, Sarawak, yang mengorbankan lima orang, kata Menteri Kesihatan Dzulkefly Ahmad hari ini.
Dzulkefly berkata perkhidmatan itu, yang dimulakan pada 1970-an, amat penting untuk menyediakan liputan penjagaan kesihatan kepada masyarakat di kawasan pedalaman negara.
"Kita akan teruskan dengan menggandakan usaha dan memperkasa perkhidmatan ini," katanya dalam satu sidang media.

Sebuah helikopter BO-105 sedang dalam penerbangan dari Lapangan Terbang Miri ke Long Lellang semalam apabila ia terhempas berhampiran STOLport Long Lellang. Semua lima penumpang, terdiri daripada empat petugas Kementerian Kesihatan dan seorang juruterbang, terbunuh.
Terdahulu, Senator RA Lingeshwaran menggesa supaya semua helikopter model yang sama digantung operasinya serta-merta buat sementara waktu, sementara menunggu pengesahan punca nahas.
Dzulkefly turut berkata operasi FDS sentiasa dikontrakkan kepada syarikat swasta, kerana kementerian tidak memiliki helikopter untuk perkhidmatan itu.
Beliau berkata kementerian sedang mengumpulkan rekod penyelenggaraan helikopter yang terhempas itu, yang akan diserahkan tidak lama lagi, dan helikopter tersebut menjalani penyelenggaraan rutin.
“Daripada situ, kita akan menentukan sama ada helikopter-helikopter ini boleh terus digunakan untuk perkhidmatan ini,” tambahnya.

Dzulkefly berkata operasi mencari dan menyelamat di lokasi nahas, yang bermula pagi ini, sedang dijalankan di bawah kendalian polis Sarawak dan bomba, dan Hospital Miri bersiap sedia untuk menerima jenazah mangsa.
Beliau berkata kementerian akan memastikan keluarga mangsa menerima bantuan, termasuk bantuan kewangan, serta sokongan kesihatan mental dan psikososial.
3ef921f4f1e1b281: IPOH, Sept 9 — Perak has denied an allegation that Taiping Hospital has no house officers (HOs), describing the claim in an article published by CodeBlue as inaccurate.

Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the hospital currently has 93 house officers out of 231 training slots allocated, giving it a 40.3 per cent placement rate.
He said the figure meant there was a shortfall of 138 house officers against the available training slots, but stressed that it was incorrect to claim that the hospital had none.

“We accept the fact that we have filled only 40.3 per cent of the housemanship slots. That is the fact, but to say there are zero house officers is not the truth,” he told a press conference on the sidelines of the State Legislative Assembly sitting here.
Sivanesan said he had met the Taiping Hospital director and obtained clarification on the hospital’s current staffing situation.
According to the hospital, there are currently 219 medical officers (MOs) serving there, comprising 137 permanent MOs, 62 contract MOs and 20 MOs who have completed their housemanship training.

He said another 46 MO positions remained unfilled based on the hospital’s current operational requirements, which include patient management, receiving referral cases from hospitals within the northern Perak cluster and managing acute patient admissions.
“The optimum requirement for medical officers at Hospital Taiping is estimated at 273,” he said.
On housemen, Sivanesan said they could not be placed in every department and were currently confined to six departments.
“At every specialist hospital, we have housemen, but they are confined to six departments,” he said.
Sivanesan said the CodeBlue article appeared to have used photographs from Taiping Hospital’s official Facebook page, which were posted on August 13.
He said the hospital’s Facebook post contained only photographs and did not include any written statement claiming that the hospital had zero housemen.
He said the article was based on a letter submitted to CodeBlue by an individual expressing exhaustion and concern over patients.
“I am not saying everything contained in the article is untrue. I am not saying all of it is wrong. There are truths in it which we will look into,” he said.

However, Sivanesan urged the publication to verify facts with the relevant authorities before publishing reports concerning healthcare matters, saying such reports could cause unnecessary alarm among the public.
“But please, when it comes to health, ensure that you get the facts right. You can meet me. I was not consulted. You can meet the director, who was also not consulted,” he said.
“Get the feedback from the director. We have nothing to hide. This involves health,” he added.
Sivanesan said he respected CodeBlue and acknowledged that the publication had highlighted issues that could be taken into consideration and addressed.
“I have high respect for CodeBlue. They have pointed out certain things which will be taken into consideration and addressed.
“But next time, verify the facts in total before coming out with articles,” he said.
79728440fa5409ee: KUALA LUMPUR: Mixue Malaysia will absorb higher operating costs rather than raise prices, as the beverage chain steps up investment in product quality, cold-chain infrastructure and store operations while shifting from rapid expansion to sustainable growth.

The company plans to offset higher expenses through supply-chain efficiencies, economies of scale and greater use of digital technology, allowing it to maintain its affordable-price positioning without putting the cost burden on consumers or franchisees, said Wang Weilong, general manager of Mixue Malaysia.
Wang said the company remained committed to building a long-term presence in the country by growing alongside local entrepreneurs, employees, consumers and communities.
"We will keep investing in product quality, operational excellence and localisation," Wang said in a statement.

The strategy was outlined during Mixue Group's 2026 mid-year performance briefing, where senior management said the group had entered a new investment cycle focused on strengthening supply chains, in-store operations and brand intellectual property.

In Malaysia, Mixue had partnered with more than 300 local store owners as of February 2026, with 93.19 per cent being Malaysian nationals. The company also directly employs about 2,900 people, adding to employment in the country's services sector.

The Statistics Department said today that informal employment in Malaysia fell to 3.28 million people in 2025, or 19.8 per cent of total employment, from 3.45 million, or 21.8 per cent, in 2023. The services sector accounted for 56.2 per cent of informal employment.

Mixue said its shift towards sustainable growth will see the company place greater emphasis on improving the performance of its existing franchise network through training, standardised operating procedures and real-time data analytics, rather than pursuing outlet expansion at all costs.

The company will also step up halal compliance, tightening controls over raw materials, beverage preparation and store management while expanding the number of outlets certified by the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia.

Over the next three years, Mixue plans to further strengthen its cold-chain and quality-management systems, expand training for franchisees and employees, raise store operating standards and accelerate halal certification.
ff2b510258033f77: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games is keeping a close watch on severe weather and flooding in several parts of Japan, with the safety of the country's athletes and officials remaining the top priority.

Malaysia's deputy chef de mission (DCDM) Azlan Iskandar said his team is in constant contact with the Asian Games organisers in Japan to obtain the latest updates on the situation on the ground for the Games on Sept 19-Oct 4.

"We received an update this morning and are in constant contact with the Asian Games team there. We will continue to receive updates throughout the day, but it is still too early and we need to assess the situation on the ground," he said during a visit to the Academy Badminton Malaysia (ABM) on Wednesday.
Japan issued a level five emergency warning on Tuesday, the highest level, following heavy rain and flooding in several areas of Aichi, where the Games are being held, and Gifu prefectures.
The warning was issued after the water level of the Shonai River, which flows through both prefectures, rose, prompting authorities to urge residents to evacuate to higher and safer ground.
Azlan, the 2010 Asian Games squash gold medallist, said his team would nevertheless not take the developments lightly and would continue to gather information before deciding on any further action.
"It is an environmental issue. The flooding was caused by rain. I was actually in Tokyo last weekend and there was heavy rain there.
"However, it is nothing different. Every country is facing the same situation and I am confident that the situation there will be handled well," he said.
Malaysia have set a target of six gold, seven silver and 20 bronze in Japan from 13 sports, including badminton.
It was almost similar to the Hangzhou Games haul, where Malaysia secured 6 gold, eight silver and 18 bronze three years ago.
5a73c0ca478c9dd4: SEREMBAN: The father of Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, who was involved in a helicopter crash near Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport), Ulu Baram, Sarawak, yesterday afternoon, admitted that he was still in shock over his son's death.
Bee Sham Ahmad, 59, who lives in Senawang, said he initially thought the incident had not resulted in any loss of life.
"I found out about the incident at 5.15pm after being informed by my eighth child.

"At first, I thought it was just a normal accident and that there had been no fatalities because there have been similar incidents before, but all the passengers survived," he said when contacted today.
Bee Sham said he contacted one of Zainol's colleagues who was serving with his son in Miri before receiving confirmation of the incident.
"I still cannot accept the news. He was too young. I still cannot believe that he has left us," he said tearfully.
Recalling his last conversation with his son, Bee Sham said Zainol had spoken to his mother by telephone for almost an hour a day before the incident.
"As usual, he would speak to us over the phone. He spoke to us as he normally did, and it was his routine to fly the helicopter whenever there was a call.
"Becoming a pilot had been his ambition since he was in school, and he was already working at the age of 21," he said.
He described Zainol, who was the fourth of 12 siblings, as a good, cheerful and responsible son.
He said he and his wife last met Zainol during the Negri Sembilan state election last month, when he returned home to fulfil his responsibility as a voter.
He said he, his wife, three children and Zainol's in-laws were flying to Miri, Sarawak, today and hoped everything would proceed smoothly.
"I was informed that the body is still at the scene. We hope to bring his remains home to be buried in Negri Sembilan," he said.
He also said DNA samples would be taken upon their arrival in Miri for the purpose of identifying the body.
It was reported that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including its pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang STOLport yesterday.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said it received notification of the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm.
c205b44367928fec: PUNCAK ALAM: Police believe that the 44-year-old man rescued by police in July after being kidnapped over a RM7 million ransom demand has links to the suspected mastermind behind a RM2.4 billion drug laboratory busted recently.

Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director, Datuk Hussein Omar Khan, said investigations uncovered links between the man and the alleged mastermind, who was shot dead during a police operation in Seremban recently.

"We established that the man has ties to the individual who was shot dead in Seremban and the syndicate, which was crippled following the raid on the drug lab at Eco Business Park V last month," he told reporters today.
6dc951862e249a45: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application for clemency when it meets this week, according to sources cited by Free Malaysia Today (FMT).

FMT reported that sources familiar with the matter said Najib’s application was expected to be among the issues raised at the board’s meeting, although it remained unclear whether the meeting would result in a decision or merely a discussion.

A separate source told the online news portal that Najib could potentially be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, although it was unclear whether the option would be considered at the meeting.
The development comes as Pakatan Harapan (PH) reiterated that individuals convicted of corruption or abuse of power, particularly in high-profile cases, should serve their sentences in full.
In a statement issued after midnight by its secretariat council, PH said it supported the Madani government’s efforts to combat corruption, leakages and abuse of power.

It said those convicted of corruption or abuse of power must fully serve the sentences imposed by the courts, while ongoing judicial processes should be allowed to run their course without creating any perception of outside influence.
The coalition did not name Najib or any specific case in the statement.

FMT reported that the statement came amid reports that the Pardons Board was expected to meet on Sept 11 to consider several matters, including Najib’s pardon application relating to his convictions linked to the 1MDB scandal.

Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
The Pardons Board subsequently halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib later withdrew his appeal against the decision.
FMT also reported that it had sought comments from Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh, Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar and Najib’s lawyer Shafee Abdullah.
3d7a0af348743069: MUMBAI: Indian conglomerate Adani Group said Wednesday that its airport unit would raise about US$1 billion selling a minority stake to a group of investors including Singapore's Temasek and US firm BlackRock.

The transaction will see investors buy a 5.54% stake in Adani Airport Holdings (AAHL), one of India's largest private airport operators, giving it a "pre-money equity valuation" around US$18 billion, a statement said.
The deal "represents one of the largest primary equity investments from financial institutions in India's airport infrastructure sector", it added.
Investors will subscribe to new equity shares of Adani Airport in three tranches, with the final leg expected to be completed by July 2027.
The money raised will be used to expand and modernise airport infrastructure, while scaling other businesses like ground-handling.
"We will continue to build capabilities within AAHL to scale it into the world's largest airports platform," Arun Bansal, chief executive of Adani Airport, said in a statement.

"This ambition is buoyed by the exponential growth opportunities across India, the rising spending power of the Indian consumer, and the momentum of our cityside developments as powerful economic catalysts in the country's major urban centres."
The fundraise comes as India's aviation sector is in the spotlight, with top two carriers Air India and IndiGo having faced several regulatory and safety challenges.

Indian airlines are expected to carry an additional 425 million passengers by 2044 - more than double last year's figure - but experts fear the growth has strained the system’s ability to cater to the boom.

The investment also comes a month after billionaire-founder Gautam Adani resolved US bribery allegations - a sign that his conglomerate is winning back the faith of global investors after years of regulatory overhang.
f4578126ada6049e: KUALA LUMPUR: Technology laggards and second-tier stocks could be next in line for gains as improving earnings and operations have yet to be fully reflected in their valuations, RHB Research said.
The research house sees bigger opportunities in such stocks as Malaysia's technology sector rides the semiconductor upcycle and earnings recovery into the second half of the year.
The sector currently trades at about 25 times forward earnings, around its five-year mean, against projected earnings growth of more than 30 per cent.
This suggests share prices have yet to fully reflect the stronger earnings growth expected from the sector.
RHB Research named Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI), Pentamaster Corp Bhd, CTOS Digital Bhd, Coraza Integrated Technology Bhd and JHM Consolidation Bhd as its top picks.
MPI is benefiting from surging AI server-related demand, particularly for power semiconductors, and is expanding its artificial intelligence (AI) server-related packaging lines to 28 from 16.
Its new Suxiang facility is expected to begin operations in the second half of its current financial year, backed by an initial business pipeline of about US$30 million.
RHB Research has a target price of RM55.80 on the stock.

Pentamaster, meanwhile, is sitting on a record RM550 million order book, with growth supported by medical and AI-driven factory automation demand as well as semiconductor testing solutions for AI and high-performance computing applications.
RHB Research has a target price of RM6.32 on the company.

Among domestic-focused software and digital solutions providers, the research house prefers CTOS, saying most negatives have already been priced in and the stock is poised for a recovery as earnings momentum improves.
Its RM1.11 target price implies 73.4 per cent upside from its last closing price of 64 sen, the largest potential upside among the 12 technology stocks under the research firm's coverage.
RHB Research also singled out Coraza and JHM as its smaller-cap top picks, expecting them to benefit from a sharp earnings rebound, stronger revenue momentum and operating leverage.
It expects Coraza to deliver two consecutive years of record revenue and earnings, supported by a larger addressable market, higher-value projects, vertical integration and a broader customer base.
The firm has a target price of RM1.45 on the stock.
For JHM, the research house said the worst appeared to be behind the company, with stronger recoveries expected in its semiconductor-related sheet metal and automotive businesses.
Growth is supported by new orders from existing customers, contributions from Magna Autosystems Inc and a RM300 million Proton contract secured through its JHM Dekai Auto Lighting joint venture.
RHB Research has a target price of 64 sen on JHM.
bf0707e8d1ae058a: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia have expressed their condolences to the families of the pilot and Ministry of Health (MOH) personnel who died in a helicopter crash in Sarawak, yesterday.
Their Majesties also prayed that the entire family and next of kin of the victims be given strength and fortitude in facing the loss of their loved ones.

“We extend our Al-Fatihah and condolences to all members of the victims’ families. Their services and sacrifices will always be remembered,” said the King and Queen through a post on the Facebook of Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar today.

Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) in a statement announced that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals including the pilot crashed near the Long Lellang Short Runway Airport (STOLport), Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching, Sarawak.
CAAM received information about the incident involving the helicopter from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm.

The Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter that took off from Miri was carrying five victims, consisting of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, an assistant medical officer (PPP) and two nurses, all of whom were on official duty. — Bernama
f34bf7d5fc6d407a: KOTA BARU: Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malik had spoken to his wife, Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, just befor she boarded a helicopter for a remote area, never knowing it would be their last conversation.
A few hours later, the 37-year-old teacher received a call from the Health Ministry informing him that his wife had been involved in a helicopter crash and had died.
"Before she departed, my wife called to tell me she would be taking a helicopter to a remote area," he said.
Dr Ainul, 32, was among the five people travelling in a helicopter that crashed and caught fire near Long Lellang STOLport, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, yesterday.
Faiz, who is also a teacher, said his wife had taken a helicopter to a remote area a day before the incident but had to turn back due to haze.
"Almost every day, my wife would take a helicopter to provide medical services to residents in remote areas.
"I was lost for words when I was informed of what had happened to my wife, and until now, I have been unable to read reports about the incident.
"This is a heavy test for our family, and we are currently staying at a hotel in Miri. We will also be updated on the latest developments from time to time.
"I will also not be taken to the crash site as a helicopter is required to get there," he said.
Faiz only hoped that all matters involving his wife and the other victims would be made easier and that his family would be given the strength to face the ordeal.

Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, had crashed near the Long Lellang Short Takeoff and Landing Port (STOLport) in Sarawak.
CAAM said it received notification of the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm.
Besides Dr Ainul, the four other victims were identified as Captain Zainol Afiq, PPP Alexson Adit, SN Debra Moset and SN Jessie Paya.
0c8fc1a17f18f5f0: PARIS: Iran launched fresh attacks against the US on Wednesday in retaliation for US strikes on its vessels.
Here are the latest developments in the conflict:
Oil prices climb
Oil prices climbed on Wednesday to near US$100 a barrel in Asian morning trade, as the Middle East war threatened to further choke supply from the crude-rich region.
The price of Brent crude, the benchmark international contract, rose to US$99.46 per barrel, while the main US contract West Texas Intermediate was at US$94.45 per barrel.
Iran attacks US vessels in Hormuz
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they attacked two US vessels, eight oil tankers and 10 "non-compliant vessels" trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, state media reported.

"Two US vessels, eight oil tankers, and 10 non-compliant vessels attempting to pass through the prohibited and unsafe zone of the Strait of Hormuz were targeted," the Guards said in a statement published by the official IRNA.
Iran strikes US base in Jordan
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they struck a US military base in Jordan with missiles in retaliation for US strikes on Tehran's vessels.
Minutes later, Jordan's army said it shot down 18 missiles from Iran targeting the kingdom.
Iran threatens tankers off Kuwait, Bahrain
Iran said Wednesday it would target oil tankers off Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for US strikes on its vessels, urging crews to leave their ships, according to the IRNA state news agency.

"We warn all oil tankers in the Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports, which host these terrorists and are partners in their evils, whether they are anchored or docked -- we warn them to leave their vessels because they will be targeted," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement posted on IRNA.
US destroys Iran oil tankers
US forces destroyed five Iranian oil carriers on Tuesday after Tehran launched ballistic missiles at an American warship twice in recent days, the US military said.

"American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable," US Central Command said in a statement, adding the strikes were "in response to Iran's most recent failed attacks".
US strikes Iran tanker
Iran's Tasnim news agency said "a small Iranian tanker was targeted by a missile attack" from the US, around six kilometres off Kharg Island.
It came after local media reported that several blasts were heard on the Gulf island, where the majority of the country's oil is exported from.
Iranian media also reported two explosions in the southern port of Jask.
Iran threatens US bases
The chief of staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, Ali Abdollahi, on Tuesday warned Tehran would attack US bases in the region if Iranian oil tankers were hit.

"The US aggressor army has given Iranian oil tankers an evacuation warning to hit them, so I announce that any attack on Iranian oil tankers will result in the targeting of US bases in the region by the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran," Abdollahi said, according to state TV.
Rubio blames Iran for Yemen fighting
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that "the Iranian hand" was behind attacks launched by Yemen's Houthi rebels against Saudi Arabia.

"The Houthis in many ways are agents and proxies of the Iranians. I think behind some of this is clearly the Iranian hand," Rubio said in response to a question about the wave of attacks, which wounded dozens.
The Houthis have launched a new offensive to seize land near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which controls entrance to the Red Sea, as the Yemeni civil war reignited after a four-year ceasefire.
Guards say seized submarine drone
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in a statement carried by state TV that they captured "one of the most modern, unmanned" US submarines.
The US military said one of its underwater drones "malfunctioned" and was not carrying any sensitive data.
Iran thwarts drone attack
Iran said in another statement carried by state TV that they thwarted a drone attack on Tuesday.
The advanced MQ1 drone -- used by only a few countries, including the US -- was "destroyed" over the Strait of Hormuz, the Guards said, without specifying who was behind the attack.
US sanctions Iran airlines
Washington imposed sanctions on "all remaining Iranian airlines" that have yet to face such penalties, as Washington pushes to step up economic pressure on Tehran.
The US Treasury Department said its latest action takes aim at "36 targets for supporting Iran's aviation sector, which the regime uses to move weapons, personnel, and illicit cargo".
59bee3cc3f94a47d: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Rescue teams are working to evacuate victims of the helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, with the operation beginning at 7.30 am today, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said.
He said the operation was being carried out by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM).
Dzulkefly said hospitals in Miri were also fully prepared at all levels to receive the victims once they were evacuated from the crash site.
“As of this morning, the evacuation operation is being carried out by the rescue teams, namely the Royal Malaysia Police and the Fire and Rescue Department,” he told a press conference here today.
Also present were Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab and Deputy Health director-general (Public Health) Dr Ismuni Bohari.
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly said the MOH always takes into account input from the authorities on technical and aviation safety aspects before making any decision on the use of helicopter assets for FDS.
He also confirmed that the healthcare personnel who died in the helicopter crash were carrying out routine FDS duties when the incident occurred.

Meanwhile, when asked about flight approval for FDS operations, Dr Mahathar said every movement of an aircraft or helicopter must comply with the prescribed safety procedures before permission to fly is granted.
He said the decision on whether a flight is allowed to operate is subject to approval by the relevant agencies and does not fall under the jurisdiction of the MOH.
“Whether permission to fly is granted or not is subject to approval by the relevant agencies, not the MOH,” he said.

Elaborating, Dr Mahathar explained that FDS operations comprise several components, including scheduled services carried out periodically according to the needs of residents in rural areas, as well as emergency medical evacuation (medevac) services to transport critically ill patients for treatment.

He said medevac missions would continue to be carried out whenever there was an urgent need to transport patients, subject to flight approval after taking into account safety assessments and prevailing weather conditions.
“However, as for scheduled services, the MOH will review the matter and, from time to time, provide input to the team on the ground,” he said.

A pilot and four MOH personnel were confirmed dead after the BO-105 flying doctor services helicopter they were travelling in crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, Sarawak, yesterday. — Bernama
b09b5e9173d8413e: KOTA BARU: The family of Dr Ainul Baraah has been asked to provide DNA samples to identify her remains.
Her father, Kamaruddin Salleh, 69, said police had contacted the family last night to inform them of the request.

Dr Ainul, 32, died when the Flying Doctor Service helicopter she was on crashed near an airstrip at Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, in the Sarawak interior yesterday. (LINK: https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/09/1528357/updated-flying-doctor-service-helicopter-crashes-near-sarawak-stolport)

So far, she is the only confirmed fatality. The authorities have yet to confirm the status of four others on the Bo-105 helicopter, which included the pilot, an assistant medical officer and two staff nurses.
Kamaruddin, a retired teacher, will depart for Sarawak today for the victim identification process.
He said that apart from DNA samples from the family, police have also asked them to bring personal items used by his daughter.
"I've gathered her toothbrush and comb, which I will give to the police. They said the DNA test will be conducted once I arrive," said Kamaruddin, who is currently with his in-laws in Bangi.
"I will leave for Sarawak this afternoon," he said.
However, he said he was not told of Dr Ainul's husband's whereabouts.
"I don't know if he has gone to the location or is waiting in Miri.
"However, some family members have left for Sarawak this morning," he said.
Kamaruddin said the family is also discussing where she should be laid to rest.
"We will do what is best and hope that our affairs are eased. We don't know yet if she will be buried there or in Kelantan," he said.
f3d0b23bb458e8ec: KUALA LUMPUR: Earnings among Malaysian technology companies more than tripled in the second quarter as stronger factory loadings began feeding through to profits amid the semiconductor upcycle.
RHB Research said aggregate core earnings among the 12 technology companies under its coverage surged 206 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM154.5 million from RM50.5 million in the preceding quarter.
The rebound came despite aggregate earnings remaining 25.8 per cent lower than a year earlier, dragged mainly by weakness among electronic manufacturing services (EMS) players.
Excluding the EMS outliers, sector earnings would have risen 21.7 per cent year-on-year, reflecting what RHB Research described as a broad-based recovery and semiconductor upcycle.

Eight of the 12 companies tracked by RHB Research delivered earnings within expectations in the second quarter, while Inari Amertron Bhd and Cnergenz Bhd were the key outperformers on stronger revenue and margins.
SKP Resources Bhd and VS Industry Bhd missed forecasts due to weaker-than-expected revenue and margins, reflecting an unfavourable product mix and higher input costs.
RHB Research cut its overall financial year 2026 (FY26) sector earnings forecast by 2.8 per cent, mainly due to weaker projections for SKP Resources and VS Industry.
However, excluding EMS players, it raised its aggregate FY26 and FY27 earnings forecasts by 2.5 per cent and 5.1 per cent respectively.
The research house maintained its "overweight" call on the technology sector and expects the bullish momentum to continue into the second half of the year.
This will be supported by improving earnings, positive management guidance and robust order books and factory loadings.
It said healthy backlogs, high loadings, steady project execution and accelerating billings should sustain earnings growth during the seasonally stronger second half.
Artificial intelligence (AI)-led demand remains a key catalyst, with heavy investment increasingly filtering through different parts of Malaysia's semiconductor supply chain.
RHB Research said strong demand for wafer fabrication equipment and automated test equipment (ATE) continued to benefit ATE and engineering support players.
Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (Osat) companies were also seeing stronger earnings from higher loadings.
Capital expenditure linked to AI and data centre buildouts, alongside continued growth in power-management and automotive integrated circuits, is also supporting the recovery.
Looking ahead, RHB Research said ATE and engineering support companies are sitting on record backlogs while Osat players are seeing record revenue and loadings.
EMS remains the exception, with the research house maintaining a neutral outlook as the segment bottoms out.
It expects higher seasonal demand in the second half to lift utilisation and aid margin recovery, with new project transfers and mass production contributing more meaningfully by FY27.
9526c2645a8f43db: SINGAPORE, Sept 9 — National authentication system Singpass has expanded its passkey feature to Android users, extending a security upgrade first rolled out to Apple iPhone users as part of Singapore’s push to reduce phishing scams.

The Straits Times reported that the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech), the government agency that operates Singpass, began notifying Android users today to create their passkeys through the Singpass app.
GovTech said the passkey system uses a unique pair of encryption keys — one stored on the user’s device and the other on Singpass’ backend — to ensure access is granted only to legitimate websites.

The agency added that passkeys cannot be shared or exploited, unlike passwords or QR codes, and will not work on fake websites because the private key on the device must match the public key registered with Singpass.
GovTech said about 800,000 iPhone users have created their passkeys since the feature launched in July.

Singpass supports 5.5 million users and is integrated with more than 1,400 government and private‑sector services, including HealthHub, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore’s tax portal, the Central Provident Fund Board, DBS Bank and Singtel.
Users must complete a one‑time registration to enable passkey authentication.
Android users need to update their Singpass app, tap the “create passkey” banner and follow the instructions to activate the feature.
Once registered, users log in to Singpass‑enabled websites by scanning their face or fingerprint, or by entering their six‑digit passcode if biometric authentication is not enabled.
Singpass’ backend system verifies the private key stored on the device against the public key registered in the system for every login attempt.
Users do not need separate passkeys for each website.
GovTech said laptops and desktops do not yet support Singpass passkeys, but the feature will be extended to desktop users by the end of 2026.

Singpass passkeys comply with open standards developed by the Fast IDentity Online (Fido) Alliance, whose members include Microsoft, Google, Apple and government bodies in Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States.
Many online services from Apple, Google, Microsoft and Adobe already support Fido passkey authentication alongside passwords and two‑factor verification.

Phishing cases in Singapore fell to 3,104 in the first half of 2026, down from 3,772 in the same period in 2025, while monetary losses dropped from S$30 million (RM105 million) to S$9.6 million (RM33.6 million).
b1196a4f6870cb38: PUNCAK ALAM: Police have crippled a syndicate that laced vape liquid with drugs before distributing it via courier services.
Seven men and two women aged between 19 and 33 were arrested in five raids across the Klang Valley under Op Melanoplus, leading to the seizure of various drugs worth RM10.82 million.

Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the drugs seized in the Aug 21 operation included 61.26kg of liquid MDMA, 11.13kg of cannabis, 6.09kg of cannabis flowers, 3.8kg of Erimin 5 pills, 3.25kg of methamphetamine and 790g of ecstasy pills.
Police also seized 959 cartridges containing liquid MDMA, 870g of cannabis biscuits, 490g of ketamine and 480g of MDMA powder.
"The syndicate's modus operandi was to mix drugs into vape liquid before distributing it to buyers through courier services," he told a press conference.
Hussein said the syndicate had been operating since April, adding that the seized drugs could have supplied an estimated 44 million users.
"Police also seized assets worth RM356,744 under the Dangerous Drugs (Forfeiture of Property) Act.
"The assets included three vehicles — a Nissan GT-R, Honda City and Proton Exora — various jewellery, and RM1,026 in cash," he said.

Hussein said the first three suspects were charged under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act for trafficking on Sept 3, while the fourth suspect was charged under Section 39A(2) of the same Act for possession on Aug 28.
Section 39B carries the death penalty or life imprisonment with a minimum of 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.
Section 39A(2) carries life imprisonment or a minimum of five years in jail, along with at least 10 strokes of the rotan.
"The seventh, eighth and ninth suspects were detained under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act, while the fifth and sixth suspects were released on police bail.
"Urine tests showed the first, second, fourth and eighth suspects tested positive for THC, while the sixth suspect was positive for ketamine," he said.
Background checks revealed that the first and third suspects had previous drug-related criminal records.

e03129f707b3f48e: Far-right parties, Maga ideology and Kremlin money are conniving to suffocate liberal idealism for another generation Not all that long ago, Europe was a beacon of liberal idealism. One memoir recalls it as an era “comfortably saturated with confidence in the unfailing and binding power of tolerance and conciliation”. The economic system seemed obviously preferable to barbarous alternatives. “People honestly believed that the divergencies and the boundaries between nations and sects would gradually melt away into a common humanity,” the author added. Those words could describe the spirit of globalisation at the turn of the millennium. They were written in the 1930s by Stefan Zweig, reflecting on the optimism of late 19th-century Vienna from the perspective of a Jewish émigré whose world had been destroyed by murderous nationalism. Zweig took his own life in 1942. He never saw fascism defeated. He couldn’t have imagined a renaissance of liberalism in the second half of the 20th century so complete as to attain a pitch of complacency rivalling the one he remembered from his childhood. 8c3e8bfe7cc488cb: PETALING JAYA: Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan (LPWP) dijangka membincangkan permohonan pengampunan bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak dalam mesyuarat minggu ini, menurut sumber.
Sumber memberitahu FMT, permohonan Najib dijangka antara perkara akan dibangkitkan dalam mesyuarat itu.
Bagaimanapun, belum jelas sama ada mesyuarat itu akan membuat keputusan atau sekadar membincangkan permohonan tersebut.

Satu lagi sumber berkata, ada kemungkinan Najib dibenarkan menjalani baki hukumannya sebagai tahanan rumah, namun belum dapat dipastikan sama ada pilihan itu akan dipertimbangkan dalam mesyuarat berkenaan.

Perkembangan itu berlaku ketika perhatian kembali tertumpu kepada usaha Najib mendapatkan pengampunan, dengan Pakatan Harapan (PH) hari ini menegaskan mereka yang disabitkan kesalahan rasuah atau salah guna kuasa, khususnya dalam kes berprofil tinggi, perlu menjalani hukuman sepenuhnya.
Dalam kenyataan dikeluarkan selepas tengah malam oleh Majlis Sekretariatnya, PH berkata gabungan itu menyokong usaha kerajaan Madani memerangi rasuah, ketirisan dan salah guna kuasa.

PH berkata, sebagai gabungan yang sejak awal memperjuangkan reformasi institusi, tadbir urus baik dan menolak rasuah, mana-mana individu yang disabitkan kesalahan rasuah atau salah guna kuasa, terutama dalam kes berprofil tinggi, perlu menjalani sepenuhnya hukuman ditetapkan mahkamah.
Gabungan itu turut berkata, proses kehakiman yang sedang berjalan perlu dibiarkan berlangsung sehingga selesai tanpa menimbulkan sebarang persepsi bahawa ia dipengaruhi pertimbangan lain.
PH tidak menamakan Najib atau mana-mana kes tertentu dalam kenyataan itu.

Kenyataan itu dibuat susulan laporan bahawa LPWP dijangka bermesyuarat pada 11 Sept untuk mempertimbangkan beberapa perkara, termasuk permohonan pengampunan Najib berhubung sabitannya berkaitan skandal 1MDB.
Sin Chew Daily melaporkan Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (Wilayah Persekutuan) Hannah Yeoh, yang menganggotai lembaga itu, memberi taklimat kepada Majlis Presiden PH pada malam Selasa.

Najib, 72, disabitkan kesalahan enam tahun lalu kerana menyeleweng RM42 juta dana SRC International. Beliau didenda RM210 juta dan dijatuhi hukuman penjara 12 tahun yang mula dijalaninya di Penjara Kajang sejak 23 Ogos 2022.
LPWP kemudian mengurangkan hukuman penjaranya kepada enam tahun dan denda kepada RM50 juta.
Pada 22 Dis tahun lalu, Hakim Mahkamah Tinggi Alice Loke menolak permohonan Najib untuk menjalani baki hukuman penjara enam tahun yang dikurangkan dalam kes SRC International sebagai tahanan rumah.
Najib pada mulanya merayu keputusan itu, namun kemudian menarik balik rayuannya selepas pasukan peguamnya memfailkan notis pemberhentian rayuan.
FMT sudah menghubungi Yeoh, Peguam Negara Dusuki Mokhtar dan peguam Najib, Shafee Abdullah, untuk mendapatkan ulasan.

0b0bda977dac1980: KUALA LUMPUR: FA of Selangor (FAS) wants the FA of Malaysia (FAM) to explain how its election committees were appointed ahead of the national body's Sept 17 election.

FAS has questioned whether the electoral committee and electoral appeal committee were properly constituted, while also seeking confirmation that the electoral committee chairman and deputy chairman meet the required legal qualifications.

FAS secretary general Izrin Nabil Ismail, in a letter to FAM secretary general Datuk Noor Azman Rahman sighted by Timesport, said its understanding from the records and agenda of the FAM extraordinary congress on June 4 was that the appointments of both committees were not specifically stated or made.
If FAM's position was that the appointments had been made during the congress, FAS asked the national body to clarify the basis and procedure under which they were made.

FAS said this was important as the 2026 Electoral Code stipulates that the electoral committee must comprise a chairman, deputy chairman, at least one ordinary member and two substitute members, with the appointments made by congress upon the proposal of the executive committee.
FAS also pointed to the electoral appeal committee, which is responsible for hearing appeals against decisions made by the electoral committee.

The association warned that any uncertainty over the appointment or composition of either committee could potentially raise questions over the validity of the election process and the rights of members or candidates to seek remedies or lodge appeals.
FAS has also asked FAM to confirm that the electoral committee chairman and deputy chairman fulfil Article 4(5) of the Electoral Code, which states that both must be "qualified to practise law".
The issue also puts the spotlight on Professor Datuk Dr Abdullah Mohamad Said, who has chaired the FAM electoral committee since 2020 and had his mandate extended by congress last year.
Abdullah is currently overseeing the election process and recently signed the official nomination acceptance letters issued to candidates contesting the Sept 17 poll.

FAS wants FAM to clarify the scope of the legal qualification requirement, including whether it refers to an individual admitted as an Advocate and Solicitor of the High Court of Malaya and possessing the necessary status to practise law.

FAS said it was aware of "widespread discussions and questions" in the media and public over the eligibility of the individual serving as electoral committee chairman, but stressed that it did not intend to draw any conclusions on the matter.
Instead, it said official confirmation from FAM was necessary to dispel doubts and safeguard the integrity of the election process.

FAS described the issues raised as more than administrative matters, saying they concerned the integrity, transparency and validity of the election that will determine FAM's leadership for the coming term.

It has asked FAM to provide written confirmation before the election process begins, saying early clarification would prevent confusion and potential disputes while giving members and prospective candidates confidence that the polls would be conducted in accordance with the Electoral Code and FAM statutes.

The letter was also copied to FAS president Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah's private secretary, Asian Football Confederation (AFC) general secretary Datuk Seri Windsor John and AFC deputy general secretary Vahid Kardany.
66c28b164ceb1fef: MELAKA: State Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh says discussions on political cooperation will only begin after the legislative assembly is dissolved.

1c281828a1903ea5: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Rapid KL will begin phased track replacement works on the Kelana Jaya Line from Sunday, with affected stations starting services at 9.30am on designated Sundays instead of the usual 6am.
The works involve replacing existing tracks with new ones, along with related maintenance activities to ensure the line’s infrastructure remains safe and reliable.
The track replacement will be carried out in seven phases and is expected to be fully completed by September 2027.
Rapid KL said areas with long curved track sections require more time for replacement, with works on the specified dates extending into the morning to allow the work to be completed properly.
The affected stations and dates are:
Phase 1: Sept 13, 20 and 27, 2026 — Taman Melati and Gombak
Phase 2: Nov 15, 22 and 29, 2026 — Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum
Phase 3: Jan 10, 17 and 24, 2027 — Dato’ Keramat, Jelatek and Setiawangsa
Phase 4: March 14, 21 and 28, 2027 — Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum
Phase 5: May 9, 16 and 23, 2027 — Masjid Jamek, Dang Wangi, Kampung Baru, KLCC and Ampang Park
Phase 6: July 11, 18 and 25, 2027 — Taman Jaya, Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum
Phase 7: Sept 12, 19 and 26, 2027 — Taman Melati and Gombak
Rapid KL said trains at stations not affected by the track replacement works would operate as usual according to their daily operating schedules.

At affected stations, ticket machines will be temporarily unavailable until 9.30am, although passengers can purchase tickets at station counters. Rapid KL and Touch ‘n Go product users can continue their journeys as usual.
Free shuttle buses
Rapid KL will provide free shuttle buses connecting the affected stations throughout the track replacement works to help passengers continue their journeys.
Station staff, auxiliary police and Prasarana Troopers will also be stationed at the affected and relevant interchange stations to assist passengers.
Signboards and information leaflets will be provided as additional guidance.

Rapid KL advised Kelana Jaya Line passengers, particularly those travelling on the affected Sunday mornings, to check for the latest information on the work schedule, affected stations and alternative services via myRapid or Rapid KL’s official social media channels.
The operator said the track replacement works were necessary to maintain the safety and reliability of the Kelana Jaya Line and support more reliable rail services in the future.
