5a7da4f025cd0883: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The government will provide all necessary assistance and support to the families of the five victims killed in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim gave the assurance in a Facebook post today.
Anwar said he was deeply saddened by the crash involving a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter carrying four Health Ministry (MOH) personnel and a pilot yesterday afternoon.
“My thoughts and prayers, as well as (my wife) Azizah’s, are with the families of all the victims as they go through this extremely difficult time.
“May they be given strength and resilience. I urge everyone to give the families space and refrain from speculation while awaiting verified information from the authorities,” he said.

Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching.

The Health Ministry also confirmed that the helicopter, which departed from Miri, was carrying a medical officer, an assistant medical officer and two nurses on official duty, in addition to the pilot.
Among the victims identified by their families were Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 31, and Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 32. — Bernama
11c06034ff8b2fbd: KUALA LUMPUR: The Flying Doctor Service (FDS) will continue despite the helicopter crash in Ulu Baram, Sarawak, that killed five people, health minister Dzulkefly Ahmad said today.
Dzulkefly said the service, which began in the 1970s, was essential to providing healthcare coverage for communities in the country's interior.
"We will continue the service by doubling down on it. We will strengthen the service," he told a press conference here.

A BO-105 helicopter was flying from Miri Airport to Long Lellang yesterday when it crashed near the Long Lellang STOLport. All five people on board, comprising four health ministry personnel and a pilot, were killed.
Senator RA Lingeshwaran subsequently called for the immediate, temporary grounding of all helicopters of the same model, pending confirmation of the cause of crash.
Dzulkefly also said that FDS operations had always been contracted to private companies, as the ministry does not own helicopters for the service.
He said the ministry was gathering the crashed helicopter's maintenance history, which would be provided to him soon, and that helicopters used for the service undergo routine maintenance.
Health director-general Dr Mahathar Abdul Wahab said the ministry would await input from the relevant authorities on the safety of helicopters currently used for the service.
"From there, we will decide whether these helicopters can continue to be used for this service," he added.

Dzulkefly said search and rescue operations at the crash site, which began this morning, were ongoing under the Sarawak police and fire and rescue department, and that Miri Hospital was on standby to receive the victims' bodies.
He said the ministry would ensure that the victims' families received assistance, including financial aid, through its Sports and Welfare Club, as well as mental health and psychosocial support.
Post-trauma support is also being extended to health ministry personnel from the FDS fraternity affected by the crash, he added.
d7df015bc127f298: KUALA LUMPUR: Affluent and high-net-worth investors in Malaysia are among the world's biggest adopters of artificial intelligence (AI) for financial and investment purposes, HSBC Bank Malaysia Bhd said.
However, more than half still prefer a combination of AI and human expertise when making financial decisions, according to the bank's latest survey.

The survey found that 85 per cent of Malaysian respondents use AI for financial and investment purposes, placing Malaysia among the top three markets surveyed, alongside China at 85 per cent and just behind India at 86 per cent.
The study, conducted by Ipsos Asia Ltd for HSBC, covered 9,993 affluent and high-net-worth investors across 10 markets.
Despite the high adoption of AI, financial professionals and institutions remain investors' leading source of investment ideas, cited by 65 per cent of respondents.
They were also the most influential factor in investment decisions at 39 per cent, more than twice the 16 per cent recorded for AI tools.
Among those who turn to financial professionals and institutions, 85 per cent cited reassurance as a key reason, while 76 per cent valued their strategic expertise.

Investors also valued their ability to spot mistakes in AI-generated data (31 per cent), provide personalised interpretations of complex information (31 per cent), and apply judgement and validation (30 per cent).
HSBC Malaysia country head of international wealth and premier banking Linda Yip said technology provided speed and efficiency, while human interaction remained essential to building trust.
She said the future of banking would depend on combining AI-driven insights with human expertise.

"By pairing advanced analytics with human relationships, we aim to support our clients with the confidence to navigate, invest and pursue growth in an increasingly complex financial landscape," she said.

Across the generations surveyed, Millennials were the heaviest users of AI for financial and investment decisions at 89 per cent, followed by Gen Z at 86 per cent, Generation X at 85 per cent and Baby Boomers at 78 per cent.
HSBC said 58 per cent of Malaysian respondents viewed a combination of human expertise and AI as their ideal approach to financial decision-making in the future.
"While AI use is high across generations, the data shows it does not remove the need for professional insights within any age group.

"For Gen Z, this includes analysing portfolio performance (61 per cent) and generating new investment ideas (57 per cent); for millennials, the pattern is similar at 53 per cent for both tasks," it said.
0379ab2638462abd: PETALING JAYA: The Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) is expected to discuss former prime minister Najib Razak’s application for clemency when it meets this week, according to sources.
Sources familiar with the matter told FMT that Najib’s application is expected to be among the matters raised at the board’s meeting this week.
However, it is unclear whether the meeting will result in a decision or whether the board will merely discuss the matter.

A separate source also said Najib could potentially be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, although it remains unclear whether the option will be considered at the meeting.

The development comes amid renewed attention on Najib’s bid for a pardon, with Pakatan Harapan (PH) reiterating today that those convicted of corruption or abuse of power, particularly in high-profile cases, should serve their sentences in full.
In a statement issued after midnight by its secretariat council, PH said it supported the Madani government’s efforts to combat corruption, leakages and abuse of power.

“As a coalition that has championed institutional reforms, good governance and rejection of corruption from the outset, PH holds that any individual convicted of corruption or abuse of power, especially in high-profile cases, must fully serve the sentence set by the court,” it said.
PH also said that all ongoing judicial processes should be allowed to run their course, “without raising any perception” of influence by other considerations.
The coalition did not name Najib or any particular case in its statement.

The statement came amid reports that the FTPB was expected to meet on Sept 11 to consider several matters, including Najib's application for a pardon in relation to convictions linked to the 1MDB scandal.
Sin Chew Daily reported that federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh, who sits on the board, briefed the PH presidential council on Tuesday night.

Najib, 72, was convicted six years ago of misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds. He was fined RM210 million and sentenced to 12 years in jail, which he has been serving at Kajang prison since August 23, 2022.
The FTPB later halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced six-year jail term in the SRC International case under house arrest.
Najib initially appealed the decision but later dropped the appeal, with his legal team filing a notice of discontinuance.
FMT has reached out to Yeoh, Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar and Najib’s lawyer Shafee Abdullah for comment.
93fb5ff986968932: SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — A video call lasting more than an hour with his mother on the night before the incident turned out to be the final moment for the family of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 31, who was involved in a helicopter crash in Sarawak yesterday.
His father, Bee Sham Ahmad, 59, said his fourth child of 12 siblings had a lengthy video call with his mother, Zaiton Muda, 59, on the night before the crash.

“He always called us, but the night before yesterday, he had a video call with his mother for more than an hour and a half, from 10 pm until after 11 pm... little did we know that it would be his last call.
“We only learned the sad news from my eighth child, who informed us that his brother had been involved in the crash yesterday afternoon,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.

Bee Sham said the last time they met was during the recent Negeri Sembilan State Election, when his son took a week’s leave to return to Senawang to vote before returning to Miri to resume his duties.

Meanwhile, he said the family was on their way to Miri, Sarawak, to undergo deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing and related identification procedures, as well as to obtain further updates on the incident.

“We were informed that all the victims are still at the crash site as it is located deep in the interior. We are still waiting for further information on arrangements to bring the remains home and, if permitted, we intend to bury him at the Forest Heights Senawang Muslim Cemetery,” he said.
Zainol Afiq leaves behind a wife and two children, aged six years and 10 months.

Yesterday, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, was reported to have crashed and caught fire near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), in a statement yesterday, confirmed the incident and said it received notification of the crash from the Flight Information Service at 3.58 pm.
Apart from Zainol Afiq, the four other victims were identified as Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, assistant medical officer Alexson Adit, and two nurses, Debra Moset and Jessie Paya. — Bernama
75447cd4fc306f0f: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's informal employment fell to 3.28 million persons in 2025, accounting for 19.8 per cent of total employment, from 3.45 million persons, or 21.8 per cent, in 2023, the Statistics Department said.

The informal sector accounted for the largest share of informal employment at 57.9 per cent, or 1.90 million persons, followed by employment in the formal sector at 41.5 per cent, or 1.36 million persons.
The remaining 0.6 per cent, or 18,300 persons, were employed in household production units, the department said in a statement today.
Men made up 61.8 per cent of informal employment, or 2.03 million persons, while women accounted for 38.2 per cent, or 1.25 million persons.

Employees represented the largest share of informal employment at 44.9 per cent, or 1.47 million persons, followed by own-account workers at 43.2 per cent, or 1.42 million persons, and unpaid family workers at 10.5 per cent, or 343,800 persons.
Within the informal sector, own-account workers accounted for the largest share at 74.6 per cent, or 1.42 million persons, followed by employees at 17.1 per cent, or 322,400 persons.
Food hawkers, internet salespersons and rubber tappers recorded the highest employment in the informal sector in 2025.
The services sector dominated informal employment, accounting for 56.2 per cent of the total.

This was mainly driven by wholesale and retail trade and the repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles, which accounted for 22.5 per cent, followed by accommodation and food and beverage service activities at 18.7 per cent.

By occupation, service and sales workers accounted for the largest share of informal employment at 38 per cent, or 1.25 million persons, followed by elementary occupations at 20 per cent, or 655,100 persons, and other occupations at 17.8 per cent, or 582,700 persons.

Selangor recorded the highest number of informal workers at 617,000, or 18.8 per cent of the total, followed by Sabah with 484,000 persons, or 14.8 per cent, and Johor with 319,800 persons, or 9.8 per cent.

For employment specifically in the informal sector, Selangor also recorded the highest share at 17.8 per cent, or 337,100 persons, followed by Sabah at 15.2 per cent, or 287,900 persons, and Johor at 10.7 per cent, or 203,600 persons.
Kelantan recorded the highest informal employment rate at 39.2 per cent, followed by Terengganu at 29.5 per cent and Kedah at 29.2 per cent.
The department said the informal sector would continue to support employment opportunities and income generation, particularly for micro-entrepreneurs and self-employed individuals.

"The government is actively formalising informal economic activities through various policies and programmes, including the Informal Entrepreneur Formalisation Plan, to increase business registrations, improve productivity, and expand access to financing, training, and social protection.
"The transition of the informal sector into the formal economy is expected to strengthen economic resilience, create higher-quality jobs, and promote inclusive growth.
"In addition, the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) provides contribution incentive schemes to encourage workers and self-employed individuals to obtain social protection coverage," it said.
b251f20301c7cba4: KULAI: A Toyota Vellfire driver was charged with the murder of a 17-year-old girl and attempting to kill four others following a road confrontation here last month.
The charges against Choo De Hui, 26, were read to him in Mandarin before magistrate R. Salini in the magistrates' court here today.
He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code with causing the teenager's death at the Persiaran Indahpura 4 roundabout between 12.20am and 12.33am on Aug 25.
If convicted, he faces the death penalty or imprisonment of up to 40 years. If not sentenced to death, he is also liable to at least 12 strokes of the rotan.

Choo was also charged under Section 307 of the Penal Code with attempting to murder four others aged between 15 and 20, at Jalan Kiambang 9 and the Persiaran Indahpura 4 roundabout during the same period.
The offence carries up to 10 years' imprisonment and a fine, or up to 20 years' imprisonment if hurt was caused.
Deputy public prosecutor Lee Weng Hong appeared for the prosecution, while Choo was unrepresented.
The court fixed Dec 2 for mention pending the completion of chemistry and post-mortem reports.

Meanwhile, in a related case at the same court, four teenagers aged between 15 and 17 pleaded not guilty to jointly committing mischief by smashing the rear windscreen and front left window of a Perodua Myvi.
They were accused of damaging the vehicle belonging to Lai Yun Zhe Jeff, 20, at the Persiaran Indahpura 4 roundabout at 12.33am on Aug 25.
They were charged under Section 426 read with Section 34 of the Penal Code for jointly committing the offence, which carries a maximum five-year jail term, a fine, or both upon conviction.
The prosecution sought RM3,000 bail for each teenager, while defence lawyer K.C. Lim requested a reduction.
The court granted bail of RM2,500 each with one surety, to be paid by their parents or guardians.
The case was fixed for mention on Oct 28 for document submission.
In the incident, the 17-year-old girl died after she was believed to have been thrown from a Perodua Myvi before being struck by the Toyota Vellfire.
The case was initially investigated as a road accident before being reclassified as murder following police investigations and statements from suspects.
3fab68ba3b954b58: PETALING JAYA: Seorang lagi juruterbang diberkas kerana dipercayai mempunyai kaitan dengan sindiket penyeludupan dadah membabitkan seorang juruterbang Malaysia Airlines ditahan bersama dadah RM45 juta di Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Soekarno-Hatta, Jakarta.

"Siasatan mendedahkan juruterbang kedua itu didakwa terlibat dalam aliran wang tunai antara sindiket berkenaan dengan seorang lagi juruterbang," katanya menurut Harian Metro.

Ini menjadikan tujuh lelaki tempatan ditahan di Malaysia berhubung kes itu, selepas enam suspek diberkas 20 hingga 28 Ogos lalu hasil soal siasat ke atas juruterbang Malaysia Airlines oleh pegawai JSJN yang dihantar ke Jakarta bulan lalu.

Empat daripada enam suspek yang dikesan melarikan diri ke Thailand dan Vietnam itu ditahan ketika kembali ke Malaysia, manakala baki dua lagi diberkas di Bukit Mertajam, Pulau Pinang dan Klang, Selangor.

Juruterbang Malaysia Airlines itu ditahan di Terminal 3 Ketibaan Antarabangsa Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Soekarno-Hatta di Tangerang pada 29 Julai lalu selepas tiba dari Kuala Lumpur dengan penerbangan MH727.
Pemeriksaan ke atas bagasinya menemui 14 bungkusan mengandungi 70,114 pil ekstasi kira-kira 25kg, selain 4g syabu dalam barang bawaannya yang semuanya dianggarkan berjumlah RM45 juta.
Menurut polis Indonesia, suspek mendakwa dijanjikan bayaran RM50,000 untuk membawa dadah itu ke Jakarta sebelum diambil individu lain dari sebuah hotel.
0ca9499ca26ade5b: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will provide all necessary assistance and support to the families of the victims of the helicopter crash in Sarawak, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

9d9db92bf77055a2: SINGAPORE, Sept 9 — Police are investigating online remarks linked to the Nepal floods and discussions about Singapore Airlines’ (SIA) investment in Air India, and have interviewed five people identified through recent reports.

Shanmugam said more than a thousand people had died and Singaporeans remained unaccounted for, yet racist comments continued to appear online.
He also pointed to “anti‑Indian, racist ranting” triggered by discussions about SIA’s investment in Air India, including “references to snakes, curry, prata, black magic.”
The Ministry of Digital Development and Information will ask social media platforms to remove comments that breach guidelines.

72b90982b283e857: KUALA LUMPUR: Industrial adhesive maker GB Bond Holdings Bhd has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at 25 sen a share, seeking to raise RM16.08 million to expand its production capacity and establish a sales presence in Vietnam.
The Penang-based company is issuing 64.3 million new shares ahead of its listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia, scheduled for Oct 1, according to its prospectus released today.
At the IPO price, GB Bond will have a market capitalisation of RM103.08 million based on its enlarged share capital of 412.3 million shares.
Of the proceeds, RM5.5 million or 34.21 per cent will be used to rent a new factory and purchase machinery and equipment, while RM3.5 million or 21.77 per cent will fund its expansion into Vietnam.
The company plans to rent a roughly 40,000-square-foot factory near its Bukit Panchor headquarters in Penang and install new production machinery there.

The expansion will lift its annual industrial adhesive production capacity by 35.31 per cent to 31,971.3 tonnes from 23,628.9 tonnes, while its sealant capacity will triple to 1,422 tonnes from 474 tonnes.
Another RM1.18 million will be used for working capital, RM900,000 to purchase equipment for product formulation and RM500,000 for marketing.
The remaining RM4.5 million will be used to defray listing expenses.
GB Bond is principally involved in the manufacturing and sale of industrial adhesives, emulsion polymers and sealants.
Its industrial adhesives, which are primarily water-based, are used in industries including paper and packaging, fabric lamination, woodworking, renovation and building materials.
Industrial adhesives are the group's main revenue contributor, accounting for RM48.71 million, or 92.89 per cent, of its RM52.44 million revenue in the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY25).
For the five months ended May 31, 2026, the segment contributed RM22.65 million, or 93.04 per cent, of the group's RM24.35 million revenue, its prospectus showed.
GB Bond's revenue rose 12.34 per cent to RM24.35 million in the five-month period from RM21.67 million a year earlier.
Profit after tax rose 17.98 per cent to RM4.55 million from RM3.86 million, while gross profit margin improved to 45.31 per cent from 42.40 per cent.
The company attributed the improved margin partly to higher sales volume, a favourable product mix and better absorption of fixed manufacturing costs.
As part of its growth plans, GB Bond intends to establish a physical presence and expand sales in Vietnam, which accounted for 4.25 per cent of its revenue in the first five months of 2026.
GB Bond has earmarked RM3.5 million from its IPO proceeds for the expansion over the next 36 months.
The IPO also includes an offer for sale of 42.88 million existing shares by managing director and promoter Datuk Gooi Ching Koay.
Together with the public issue, a total of 107.18 million shares will be offered under the IPO.
Applications for the IPO opened today and will close on Sept 18, with balloting scheduled for Sept 22 and allotment on Sept 29.
Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd is the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter and placement agent for the IPO.

136aa95e14c9dc3d: Every Merdeka, Malaysians come together in ways that feel uniquely our own.
Families gather, communities celebrate, flags fill the streets and, for a moment, differences fade into the background as the nation rallies around a shared sense of pride.
That same spirit comes alive through sport.

Whether it is the roar of a crowd behind a national athlete, children discovering their passion on the field or Malaysians from different backgrounds cheering for a sporting event, sport has a remarkable way of bringing people together.

It is this shared spirit of unity, determination and national pride that Milo is celebrating over the Merdeka weekend alongside the Youth and Sports Ministry, as Malaysia looks ahead to hosting the SEA Games in 2027.
For generations, Milo has been part of Malaysia's sporting journey, championing active lifestyles and encouraging young Malaysians to discover the champion within.

Its long-standing collaborations with the Education Ministry, Youth and Sports Ministry and Olympic Council of Malaysia, alongside grassroots programmes such as the Milo Champions Clinic and Majlis Sukan Sekolah Malaysia reflect a continued commitment to nurturing the next generation through sport.
Milo also served more than 100,000 complimentary cups of cold Milo throughout National Day and Malaysia Day festivities.
More than a refreshing drink, the cups represent an invitation to pause, connect and celebrate what Malaysians can achieve when we come together.
It is a celebration of the enduring 'Malaysia Boleh' spirit - the belief that with determination, resilience and unity, every individual can take that first step towards achieving something greater.

That spirit took centre stage at the National Day Parade in Putrajaya on Aug 31 where Milo, in collaboration with the Youth and Sports Ministry, unveiled a specially curated float celebrating Malaysia's sporting heroes and the nation's journey towards the SEA Games 2027.

Designed as a moving celebration of Malaysian sporting pride, the float brought together striking SEA Games-inspired elements, the Jalur Gemilang, iconic national landmarks and tiger-stripe motifs symbolising the spirit of Harimau Malaya.
At its centre stood a replica of the Bukit Jalil National Stadium - a powerful symbol of Malaysia's readiness to welcome the region when the country hosts the 34th SEA Games.

Following behind were the iconic Milo vans, a familiar presence at sporting events and community activities across the country, reinforcing the brand's decades-long commitment to supporting sports and active lifestyles in Malaysia.

Among the six athletes joining the Youth and Sport Ministry float are national weightlifter Mohamad Aniq Kasdan and Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin, national lawn bowler Aleena Ahmad Nawawi, national para long jumper Eljoe Gotuoh and national wheelchair basketball athlete Freday Tan Yei Bing.
Each one of them carries stories that extend beyond medals and records.
Together, they demonstrate that sporting excellence takes many forms and that every journey has the potential to inspire others to take their first step.

"Celebrating Merdeka and taking part in the National Day Parade is a truly special experience. I'm grateful to Milo for the opportunity to be part of the Ministry of Youth and Sport float and spotlight our national athletes representing Malaysia at the SEA Games 2027.

"We hope this would create greater awareness amongst Malaysians to come together and rally their support for Team Malaysia. Knowing the nation is behind us will inspire us to push our limits and give our best for Malaysia," said Mohamad Aniq Kasdan, national weightlifter.
"It is truly an honour and a deeply special moment to celebrate National Day with all Malaysians.
"Today reminds us that the strength of Malaysia lies in our unity through sports - when we stand together and share a common dream, there is no limit to what we can achieve as a nation.
"For me, there is no greater source of inspiration than hearing the roaring cheers of our fellow Malaysians. Malaysia Boleh!" said Aleena Ahmad Nawawi, national lawn bowler.
As Malaysia prepares to welcome Southeast Asia for the SEA Games in 2027, the excitement is already beginning to build for all Malaysians.
Among the crowds gathered for the National Day Parade celebrations, Bukhari, 46, reflected on how sports can bring communities together and inspire a stronger sense of belonging as Malaysians.

"For me, the true spirit of sports goes beyond competition. It is about coming together, whether cheering for the same team, celebrating a national athlete's victory or simply sharing the excitement of a sporting moment.
"Sports can unite Malaysians. When everyone comes together to watch and support, it opens up communication between people, and that's where unity comes from," he shared.

With Milo playing a role in this year's National Day Parade and supporting athletes on their journey towards the SEA Games 2027, Bukhari believes sport can continue to inspire Malaysians to stand together, regardless of age or background.
He added, "Malaysians will continue to come together and support one another, because when we cheer together and stand together, we are stronger as one Malaysia!"
His own memory with Milo is a reflection of that enduring spirit.
As a lifelong Milo drinker, Bukhari fondly recalls enjoying the drink throughout his childhood in the 1980s, whether at school or as part of his bedtime routine.

"Milo has always been part of my life, from the past to the present. I like having a cup before I sleep, and now all four of my kids follow the same routine," he said, alongside his wife and four children.
For Muhamad Hafizhuddin, 45, and Sharifah Norashikin, 46, from Segamat, Johor, Merdeka means making a wonderful journey together as a family.
The couple traveled overnight to bring their children to Putrajaya to experience the National Day Parade together - a memory they hope will last a lifetime.
Reflecting on the significance of Merdeka, Muhamad shared,
"For me, Merdeka is a special time for Malaysians to come together and celebrate our country.

"Being able to experience the National Day Parade with my family makes it even more meaningful. It was also wonderful to see how Milo continues to be part of these celebrations, and more importantly, how it promotes sports and an active lifestyle in Malaysia."
As parents, the couple hopes to instill the same spirit of energy and togetherness in their children.
"We always encourage our children to be active and play every day. We hope that as they grow, they will continue to enjoy sports and make staying active a part of their everyday lives," they said.

168015bfeb402fe6: SEPT 9 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim (the King) on Friday (Sept 4) declared, or proclaimed, an emergency in Sarawak's Serian Division due to hazardous haze conditions.
On Monday (Sept 7), the King consented to lifting the emergency in Serian.
Here are the simple steps involved in making a proclamation of emergency and subsequently revoking it.

First, the Prime Minister advises the King that a grave emergency exists whereby the security, economic life and public order in the Federation are threatened by haze causing air pollution that is hazardous to public health.

Second, acting on the advice of the Prime Minister and satisfied that such a grave emergency exists, the King, in exercise of the powers conferred on His Majesty under Article 150(1) of the Federal Constitution, proclaims that a grave emergency exists and that the proclamation extends throughout the Serian Division in Sarawak.
Third, the government publishes the proclamation in the gazette.
The gazette can be seen here.
In law, the proclamation of emergency is known as P.U. (A) 317/2026.
A gazette is an official publication of the federal or state government.

It contains, among other things: (a) proclamations bringing legislation into operation; (b) notifications of government decisions and subordinate legislation; (c) public service appointments and promotions; (d) government tenders and land acquisition notices; and (e) electoral notices.
In simple words, a gazette is a legal notification to the public of any of the above.
The gazette serves as evidence of the matters contained therein.
Therefore, if one were to raise questions as to whether the emergency in Sarawak's Serian Division was duly proclaimed by the King, P.U. (A) 317/2026 serves as evidence of the proclamation.
The three steps will similarly be followed when the emergency is ended through a separate proclamation.
The proclamation ending the emergency in Serian has indeed been published in the gazette.
It is called the Proclamation of Emergency (Serian Division, Sarawak) (Revocation) — P.U. (A) 318/2026.
The above informs us that a proclamation per se will not suffice.
The proclamation has to be published in a gazette.
Now, Negeri Sembilan’s new menteri besar, Ismail Lasim, allegedly signed a proclamation endorsing the deposition of state ruler Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
The signed proclamation was dated Aug 3 — just a day after Ismail took an oath of loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz.
This was revealed in a Sept 5 statement by the state’s four traditional chieftains, known as the Undang Yang Empat, who have the power to elect and remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

A day later, on Sept 6, Ismail responded that “the Undang Yang Empat have the right to their opinion” but that he “and the state government express full loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar”.
According to a report published by The Straits Times on Sept 8, Ismail did not confirm or deny whether he signed the proclamation.
The turn of events has been called “bizarre”.
Ismail, however, has denied claims that Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi was involved in attempts to remove Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
Even so, Ismail still holds the last card — that is, the publication of the alleged proclamation dated Aug 3 in the gazette.
As I said earlier, a proclamation per se will not suffice; it has to be published in a gazette.
Until then, in my humble opinion, Tuanku Muhriz will continue to be the state’s sovereign.
* This is the personal opinion of the writers or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
4a414532356b7842: WASHINGTON: The United States banned a broad swath of Canadian alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and dairy products from import on Tuesday, sharply escalating an already acrimonious trade spat.
The import bans, which go into effect on Sept 29 and were published on the White House's website, came after Canada's own retaliatory tariffs on US goods took effect after midnight on Tuesday.
Those Canadian levies themselves followed 50 per cent tariffs that the United States imposed on some US$20 billion of Canadian goods last month, after several rounds of negotiations collapsed.

The breakdown has widened a rift between the longtime allies, who have blamed each other for the failed talks, spurred Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to urge a further shift away from Canada's biggest trading partner, and cast doubt on the viability of the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement.
"We have everything we need to pivot and prosper," Carney said on Tuesday in a video posted on YouTube.
"That pivot will come at a cost. There's always a cost to action. But it doesn't come close to the cost of standing still," he said.

The US bans appeared to cover most alcohol products, including beer and various types of wine, whisky, bourbon, rum, vodka, vermouth, tequila, mezcal, and brandy. The dairy ban covers whey protein, invert molasses, cane molasses and non-alcoholic beer, per notices on the White House's website.

In addition to the import bans, various cheese products were added to a list of products subject to a 50 per cent tariff, but not banned outright. Some paper, aluminum, wood, furniture, lighting and other products were also added to the list.

A US official said President Donald Trump's pre-existing threat to increase tariffs on Canadian autos from 25 per cent to 50 per cent on Jan 1 remained in effect. The official added that US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer had spoken with Dominic LeBlanc, Canada's minister responsible for bilateral US trade, over the past couple of days, and the pair were expected to speak again in the coming days to see if there was an alternative path for the two countries.
In a social media post on Tuesday night, LeBlanc criticized the latest US measures and said he was in contact with Greer regarding a path forward.
"As has been the case for the last 18 months, our first priority remains on protecting and supporting Canadian workers, farmers, families, and businesses from these unjustified actions," he wrote.
OTTAWA STRIKES BACK
Ottawa's retaliatory measures, which in turn provoked Washington's move on Tuesday night, were designed to put economic and political pressure on Washington, Canadian government officials said.

Those counter-tariffs cover some US$20 billion of US goods, with duties ranging from 15 per cent to 50 per cent across products from steel and furniture to clothing and electronics, and are expected to hit sectors in some competitive states such as Michigan and Ohio, ahead of US midterm elections in November.

While the tariffs affect a small amount of exports compared with total trade between the US and Canada, some analysts worry the standoff could destabilize the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement, the free-trade pact that succeeded NAFTA. Together they have underpinned commerce across North America for decades.

"What we are worried about is an escalatory spiral," said Michael Harvey, executive director of the Canadian Agri-Food Trade Alliance and a member of Carney's advisory committee on bilateral US economic relations.
"But at the same time, we totally understand that the prime minister needs to find areas of leverage."
Trump has been lobbing various attacks at Canada on Truth Social in recent days.
On Monday, he said Canadian private jet maker Bombardier would no longer be allowed to sell its planes in the United States unless it started manufacturing in the country.

He also shared a map of North America draped in the US flag, including Canada and Mexico, and an AI-generated image reviving a running jab at Carney, calling him "Governor," a reference to his repeated taunt that Canada should become the 51st US state.

On Tuesday, hours before the latest import bans, Trump directed the General Services Administration, a US government body responsible for providing services for the federal government, to coordinate with the US Trade Representative and "REMOVE Canadian-origin products from GSA's Multiple Award Schedules unless Canada restores full and fair reciprocity for American Farmers and Companies."
VARIOUS SECTORS HIT

Trump's tariffs implemented last month hit sectors including wine, furniture, dairy products, cement, clothing, fishing rods and hockey equipment, covering US$20 billion, or 5 per cent, of Canadian exports to the US
A Sapporo spokesperson said the brewer is considering moving a limited amount of production of non-alcoholic drinks from Canada to the US due to tariff risks, but no final decision has been made.
Sapporo owns Ontario-based Sleeman Breweries. Canada accounts for more than half of the Japanese firm's overseas beer sales.

According to Canadian and US government data, Canada has shipped almost 68 per cent of total exports to the US this year, out of which roughly 80 per cent moved duty-free due to exemptions under the USMCA pact. Protections under the agreement have provided the domestic economy some resilience.
Last month's tariffs, imposed under a Depression-era US law, do not allow Ottawa to exercise USMCA exemptions.
Concerns about the USMCA's future have fueled uncertainty about investment and growth, as Canada wages a trade war against an economy 13 times its size.
Polls also show Carney has broad support from Canadians, but that could disappear within months as the consequences of the trade war sink in, according to political analysts.
A new poll from Angus Reid on Tuesday showed that approval of Carney's performance jumped 11 points to 62 per cent from an August poll.
Meanwhile, just 20 per cent of Americans approved of Trump's tariffs on Canadian goods, a Reuters/Ipsos poll found.

Trump threatened last month to raise US tariffs on all cars, trucks and automotive parts from Canada to 50 per cent starting January 1, and signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America.

3ea220366262c766: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim will remain in police custody until tomorrow under a two-day remand order to assist in a cheating investigation.

f4c047007563cb22: SINGAPORE: Singapore will raise the annual salaries of its political leaders including prime minister Lawrence Wong, reviving scrutiny of a pay system that has long been politically sensitive in the city-state.

Wong, the best-paid government leader in the world, will see his yearly pay boosted to S$3.6 million (US$2.8 million) from S$2.2 million. He told lawmakers on Tuesday he will donate the increment for the next five years.

“Political salaries are a difficult and emotive issue -- the sums involved are more than what most citizens earn,” Wong said in parliament. “It is ultimately about whether Singapore will continue to have the quality of political leadership we need to take our country forward.”

All other office holders will get a one-time salary bump of as much as 9% from Oct 15 and could take an entry-level minister’s annual income to around S$1.2 million. The adjustment will depend on individual circumstances, including performance. The median annual income for Singapore residents was S$69,300 in 2025.

The wealthy island has long justified high political salaries as necessary to attract capable people into government and reduce the risk of corruption. The system remains politically sensitive at a time of heightened economic anxiety, particularly as Wong seeks to bring more private-sector talent into politics.

Wong said he failed to persuade several corporate leaders, who were earning several times a minister’s salary, to join politics before the 2025 election. While pay wasn’t cited as a reason, that doesn’t mean remuneration is irrelevant, he added said.
“I have not given up,” Wong said. “I am still looking and I hope to persuade a few to join us in the next election.”
US President Donald Trump gets US$400,000 a year while Swiss President Guy Parmelin is paid about US$600,000.

“The bigger question is whether salary alone will be able to move the needle on recruiting better candidates in future elections,” said Nydia Ngiow, managing director for global trade and economics at strategic business advisory firm BowerGroupAsia. Wong’s decision to donate his own increment “reflects an awareness that the optics require careful management”.

Singapore has frozen political pay for the past 15 years. Annual salaries for government leaders were slashed by more than 30% following public anger over ministerial pay and widening inequality in the 2011 election. Singapore’s first prime minister Lee Kuan Yew had often defended civil-servant salaries, arguing in his autobiography From Third World to First that “underpaid ministers and public officials have ruined many governments in Asia.”

Singapore typically reviews the salaries of political office holders every five years through an independent committee, with the government last deferring its recommendations in May, citing uncertainty over the economic impact of the Middle East conflict. The government decided not to proceed with a recommended upward pay adjustment in 2017 and deferred its 2023 review.

The city state sets its benchmark salary formula for an entry-level minister at a 40% discount of the median of the top 1,000 Singaporean earners, said coordinating minister for public services Chan Chun Sing. The changes including an increase in allowance for lawmakers could cost the government as much as S$11.6 million a year, he added.
While salaries for political office holders have remained unchanged, wages elsewhere have risen, making it more difficult to attract talent from the private sector, Wong said.
“If we want our political system to remain effective, we cannot allow its basic terms of service to drift further and further away from reality,” he said.
6d05078971127648: KUALA LUMPUR: Independent pair Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani have set a lofty target of winning the men's doubles gold in Aichi-Nagoya.
World No. 6 Sze Fei-Izzuddin, despite a world-class field at the Asian Games, and the BA of Malaysia's (BAM) scratch pair Aaron Chia-Tee Kai Wun have been tasked to battle for gold on Sept 19-Oct 4.

"I feel we have a good chance although there will be many strong opponents at the Asian Games, but we are targeting high. Surely going for gold," said Izzuddin during Asian Games deputy chef de mission Azlan Iskandar's visit to the Academy Badminton Malaysia (ABM) on Wednesday.
Having won the Super 1000 Indonesia Open and Super 500 Indonesia Masters this year, Sze Fei-Izzuddin have been on a consistent run.

The duo also made it to the quarter-finals at the World Championships in New Delhi last month and remain one of the few pairs to beat South Korean world No. 1 and gold medal favourites Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae.
The Malaysians also overcame Won Ho-Seung Jae in the Indonesia Open final in June.

Sze Fei declared that they are physically and mentally ready for the battle in Japan, dispelling any fears over Izzuddin's condition after the pair were forced to concede a walkover midway through the first round at the China Masters last week.
Izzuddin was said to be in discomfort, but his confident mood at the ABM was a sign that they are well on their way to securing a first podium finish in a major event.
"So far, our condition is all good after coming back from the China Masters," said Sze Fei.

The other title contenders are defending champions and world No. 5 Satwiksairaj Rankireddy-Chirag Shetty of India, who won the China Masters, and newly crowned world champions Liang Wei Keng-Wang Chang (No. 3), as well as Indonesia's world No. 2 Fajar Alfian-Shohibul Fikri.
Asked whether Malaysia's overall six-gold target for the Asian Games is achievable, Izzuddin believes the target is well within reach.
"Every athlete will give their best, and I believe the six-gold target is realistic for the Malaysian athletes," stated Izzuddin.

Malaysia last won the men's doubles gold through Koo Kien Keat-Tan Boon Heong at the 2006 Doha Games, and if Sze Fei-Izzuddin can play to form, they can create their own piece of history in Aichi-Nagoya.
7c4777e499bc50a3: ENSENADA: The father of two Australian surfers killed in Mexico two years ago testified in court Tuesday that his life had been turned into hell, as the high-profile trial continued into its second day.

Three men are charged in the killing of Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33, respectively, and their 30-year-old American friend Jack Carter Rhoad, who were on a surfing trip to Mexico's Pacific coast in April 2024.
Authorities say the three were killed in an attempted robbery, and their bodies were found dumped in a cliff-top shaft with gunshot wounds to their heads.
"It's hell," the victims' father Martin Robinson told the court. "It's hard for a parent to lose a son, and we lost two sons."
"It’s not just the loss, but also the potential they had the dreams that lay ahead of them, the places they traveled, and the love they had for others," he said.
Robinson described the ordeal of having to identify his sons' bodies: Callum by a tattoo on his forearm, while identifying Jake was more difficult and required photographs.
Rhoad's mother Page compared the crime to an execution.
"I miss my son every day, and I don't know if I will ever be able to regain my balance," she testified. "Carter loved Mexico. He spoke fluent Spanish and loved dancing, Mexican food and its people."
Authorities say the men were killed during an attempt to steal their pickup truck, which was later found burned near their bodies.
A protected witness testified Monday that they accompanied one of the defendants to the crime scene and fled after hearing gunshots, and were later threatened into silence.
The surfers' disappearances and deaths sparked widespread outrage and grief in Australia and the United States, prompting a major social media search for their bodies.
"We hold no resentment toward the people who did this, but we cannot understand how they could have taken the lives of two beautiful people," Martin Robinson told the court.
The trial is expected to run until the end of September.
Rhoad's widow, Natalie, is scheduled to testify Wednesday.

e399cb2de2ebefdf: SINGAPORE, Sept 9 — Authorities in Palau are carrying out search‑and‑rescue operations for a Singaporean diver who disappeared during an outing in the island nation on Monday.

Singapore’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) said in a statement that it is assisting the diver’s family and coordinating with Palau officials involved in the search, according to a Straits Times report.
“We will continue to monitor the situation closely,” MFA said.
The missing diver was last seen in waters off Palau, an island nation south‑east of the Philippines known for its clear seas, coral reefs and limestone formations.
Palau comprises about 340 islands, islets and atolls, with most of its roughly 18,000 residents living in Koror, the former capital and main commercial hub.
The archipelago attracts visitors with activities such as diving, snorkelling, hiking and wildlife encounters.
Travel links to Palau have expanded in recent years, with China Airlines increasing its Taipei–Koror flights from twice weekly to four or five times a week since 2024.
United Airlines also launched a non‑stop Tokyo–Koror route in October 2025.
Several Singapore‑based dive operators and travel agencies offer packages to Palau’s waters.
According to figures from Palau’s Ministry of Finance, the country recorded 6,963 visitors in July.

039178c8df790b84: IPOH, Sept 9 — Perak is stepping up preparations for the Super El Niño phenomenon, with hospitals and clinics given the highest priority for water supplies, including a minimum 48-hour reserve in storage tanks.

Speaking at the State Legislative Assembly, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the state government was taking the phenomenon seriously, as it could bring hotter and drier weather than usual, particularly during the Southwest Monsoon from May 14 to September this year.
He said the phenomenon was expected to persist until early 2027, prompting the state government to continuously strengthen its preparedness measures.

“Through the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN), technical agencies such as the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) and Perak Water Board (LAP) are continuously monitoring and reporting weather forecasts and water levels at major dams.
“This includes Bukit Merah Dam and Sultan Azlan Shah Dam,” he said.
Saarani was responding to an oral question from Bota assemblyman Najihatussalehah Ahmad about the state government’s plans and preparedness for the Super El Niño phenomenon.
On public health, Saarani said the Perak Health Department (JKN Perak) was guided by the Health Ministry’s 2021 Action Plan for Managing Health Risks from Heatwaves.

He said four main strategies had been outlined, namely targeted health advocacy, daily surveillance of heat-related illnesses, haze and waterborne diseases, activation of the crisis preparedness and response centre if a heatwave warning was issued, and ensuring the continuity of health facility operations.
“JKN Perak, together with LAP, gives the highest priority to water supplies for hospitals and clinics, with a minimum 48-hour storage tank reserve.
“This also includes ensuring sufficient supplies of critical medicines,” he said.

In the agricultural sector, Saarani said the state government was focusing on the efficient management and distribution of water resources through major irrigation infrastructure and the mobilisation of mobile pumps for water recycling.

He said structured agricultural areas such as IADA Seberang Perak were being closely monitored due to their reliance on gravity-flow irrigation systems, which could be affected by declining water levels.
“Should the situation become increasingly critical, JPBN, together with NADMA and MetMalaysia, is prepared to coordinate cloud-seeding operations in targeted catchment areas,” he said.
On environmental measures, Saarani said DOE had activated the National Open Burning Action Plan and the Peatland Fire Operations Action Plan.
He said the department was conducting daily patrols at hotspot locations, including during the day, at night and on public holidays.

“The DOE is also using drones for monitoring and enforcing penalties under Section 29A of the Environmental Quality Act (Amendment) 2024, which provides for compounds of up to RM500,000 and fines of up to RM1 million,” he said.
Saarani said DOE was also working with local authorities, the police and the Fire and Rescue Department to prevent open burning that could worsen air quality and pollution levels.
He said DOE was also regularly monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at high-risk locations to allow early warnings to be issued promptly.

He said LAP had activated a phased mitigation plan covering the optimisation of water treatment plant operations, water supply rezoning, mobilisation of water tankers, deployment of static water tanks and the use of alternative water sources.
LAP had also applied for RM2.4 million from the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security for mitigation measures in affected areas.
“LAP is also working closely with the National Water Services Commission through a war room mechanism to proactively manage any risk of a water crisis,” he added.

Meanwhile, Saarani said the Department of Agriculture, together with the Department of Minerals and Geoscience, had updated and activated more than 100 tube wells at strategic locations to provide groundwater for crops and livestock.
He said farmers were also receiving smart agriculture training as a long-term measure to improve water-use efficiency and ensure continued production.
“This includes technical applications involving the Internet of Things (IoT) and modern farm management systems at district agricultural development training centres,” he said.
He said the state government would activate the State Disaster Operations Control Centre under JPBN if necessary to coordinate logistics and emergency water supplies.
“Daily monitoring of early warnings will also continue alongside public awareness campaigns to minimise health risks and enable immediate intervention,” he said.

a277d127d1b9b595: SYDNEY: Australian World Cup star Cristian Volpato has been fined after failing a roadside test for cocaine, police and media reports said Wednesday.
Volpato was reported in July to have allegedly tested positive for cocaine after he was pulled over for speeding in Sydney.
New South Wales police said on Wednesday that a second sample taken at the time had also tested positive.
They said a 22-year-old man -- widely identified as Italy-based Volpato by local media -- was fined Aus$722 (US$522).
His driving licence has also been suspended since July.
Volpato, an attacking midfielder for Serie A side Sassuolo, made three appearances at the World Cup after switching his international allegiance from Italy to Australia shortly before the tournament.
He was born and raised in Sydney before moving overseas and represented Italy at various youth levels.
4fc88293d30693d4: WASHINGTON: The National Transportation Safety Board said on Tuesday that evidence recovered from a flight data recorder suggested the pilots of an Amazon Prime Air cargo plane involved in a deadly crash considered aborting the landing after the aircraft touched down.
The 32-year-old Boeing 767 operated by Miami-based 21 Air overran the runway by some 1,300 feet (396 m) and crashed into two vehicles, killing five people and injuring five others on Sunday.
NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy told reporters that investigators would interview both of the pilots on Wednesday and then release details from the cockpit voice recorder.

The NTSB said 30 seconds before the end of the flight data recording, the nose landing gear and right main landing gear touched down on the runway at a speed of 158 knots (181 mph), while 19 seconds before the end of the recording, the left main landing gear touched down at a speed of 134 knots.
A few seconds later, the brakes were released and the throttles were increased to values consistent with go-around thrust, indicating a late attempt to abort the landing and get back in the air.
But 11 seconds before the end of the recording, throttles were reduced to idle power and brakes were reapplied. The final ground speed was 65 knots at the end of the recording.
The NTSB said there was no indication in the recorded data that speed brakes or thrust reversers were deployed to help slow the plane.

Homendy is leading a team of 32 investigators at Miami International Airport. She said the NTSB was able to release one of two runways closed since the accident to allow for departures from an easterly direction late on Tuesday.

The Amazon cargo plane was on its third flight of the day, coming from San Juan, Puerto Rico. It had flown from Cincinnati to Miami and from Miami to San Juan earlier on Sunday before the crash at 1:53 p.m. EDT (1753 GMT).

The captain, 55, received his type rating for the 767 in May and has 7,145 hours of flight time, while the first officer, 37, received his type rating on the 767 in April 2025 and has 2,655 flying hours, the NTSB said.
359d39c1f2177a60: WASHINGTON, Sept 9 — Singaporean Malone Lam pleaded guilty in a federal court to a racketeering conspiracy charge for leading a cryptocurrency theft ring that stole more than US$260 million (RM1.05 billion) from victims across the United States.
In yesterday’s hearing, Lam, 22, admitted organising a sophisticated “social engineering” operation that targeted people with large cryptocurrency holdings, according to a CNA report.

He and his co‑conspirators impersonated employees of trusted companies, including Google, to persuade victims to disclose passwords, seed phrases and authentication codes that unlocked their digital wallets.
“I plead guilty, Your Honour,” Lam said after a long sigh, following prosecutors’ account of how he used those stolen credentials to direct the group’s attacks.

Prosecutor Christopher Howland told the court that Lam “played multiple roles” in the scheme, which the Department of Justice considers its first bitcoin‑related case brought under the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) Act.
Lam faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison.
He told the court he is receiving therapy and medication for depression, anxiety and sleep issues.
Lam is the 11th of 18 defendants to plead guilty.
The group’s largest theft occurred in August 2024, when Lam and his associates accessed a victim’s wallet and obtained more than 4,100 bitcoin valued at about US$230 million at the time.
Authorities arrested Lam weeks later after his spending on luxury cars, private jets, security guards and high‑end rental properties drew attention.
Court filings show he bought vehicles worth up to US$3.8 million each and spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on single nights out, including US$569,000 at a Los Angeles nightclub.
Lam and his co‑conspirators attempted to launder stolen cryptocurrency by converting it into payment cards or cash.
His guilty plea followed months of uncertainty over whether he would accept a deal, with some co‑defendants prepared to testify against him if the case went to trial.
Lam is scheduled to return to court on Dec 8 for a status hearing, when a sentencing date is expected to be set.
He and his co‑conspirators have been ordered to repay more than US$245 million to victims.
ce6e5c151908364a: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu Youth chief Hilman Idham today urged the government to expedite the repeal of the Sedition Act, following his acquittal by the magistrates' court of causing public fear through a statement on social media.
Describing the law as outdated, the Gombak Setia assemblyman said it should be repealed to ensure that Malaysia continues becoming a more developed country.
"The Sedition Act is among the laws that are no longer appropriate to have in our country.

"I urge the government to repeal laws such as this. The Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) is expected to be repealed. The Sedition Act has yet to be abolished," he told a press conference at the Kuala Lumpur courts complex lobby.
The higher education ministry is working towards the repeal of Auku, which the government said would be replaced with a new legislative framework.
Magistrate Nurul Izzah Hasan Basri acquitted Hilman of the charge today after finding that the prosecution had failed to prove the elements of the offence under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code.

Hilman, 37, was charged on Aug 20 with making a statement that could cause public alarm on a TikTok account named alfah.channel.tv, which could induce a person to commit an offence against public order, at 2.09pm on July 30 last year.

Hilman was initially investigated under the Sedition Act following a speech he delivered outside the Dang Wangi police headquarters on July 29, 2025, where he protested the arrest of several party members, believed to be in connection with the Turun Anwar rally.
451be7557eb023b2: JAKARTA: Anak Krakatau meletus semula pada Rabu, ketika aktiviti gunung berapi di Selat Sunda itu terus berlanjutan susulan beberapa letusan baru-baru ini.

Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi Indonesia (PVMBG) memaklumkan letusan pada 12.47 pagi waktu tempatan itu direkodkan selama 28 saat dengan amplitud seismik maksimum 51mm, manakala ketinggian letusan tidak dapat diperhatikan.

Badan Meteorologi, Klimatologi dan Geofizik Indonesia (BMKG) berkata, analisis imej satelit Himawari-9 pada 7 pagi Rabu menunjukkan abu dari Anak Krakatau mencapai ketinggian sehingga 7,000 kaki dan bergerak ke arah barat laut, meliputi sebahagian Teluk Lampung.

"Orang ramai, khususnya mereka yang berada di sekitar selatan Lampung dinasihatkan terus berwaspada, tidak panik dan mendapatkan maklumat rasmi daripada BMKG, PVMBG, badan geologi serta pihak berkuasa tempatan,” menurut catatan terbaharunya di media sosial.
Letusan pada Rabu itu menyusul tiga letusan pada Selasa, selepas fasa letusan berterusan kira-kira 25 jam bermula 11.07 malam Jumaat reda sejurus selepas tengah malam Ahad lalu.

Anak Krakatau yang terletak di Selat Sunda antara Pulau Jawa dan Sumatera kekal pada Tahap III, tahap kedua tertinggi dalam sistem amaran gunung berapi empat peringkat Indonesia, manakala pihak berkuasa memberi amaran potensi berlaku letusan susulan masih tinggi.

PVMBG menerusi laman sesawangnya melaporkan tiga lagi gunung berapi di Indonesia turut merekodkan letusan pada Rabu, iaitu gunung Semeru di Jawa Timur meletus pada 12.15 pagi dan sekali lagi pada 5.11 pagi, namun ketinggian letusan tidak dapat diperhatikan.

Gunung Ili Lewotolok di Nusa Tenggara Timur pula meletus tiga kali pada 5.03 pagi, 5.56 pagi dan 9.51 pagi, menghamburkan abu setinggi 400 hingga 600m dari puncak yang bergerak ke arah barat laut dan barat.
Gunung Ibu di Maluku Utara meletus pada 5.27 pagi dan 9.19 pagi, dengan abu mencapai 400m dan 600m dari puncak serta bergerak ke arah timur laut dan timur.
44dd733b3d214967: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim was charged today with receiving gratification for using his position to influence a decision to invest RM190 million in a company in which he is accused of having an interest.

Azeez was alleged to have directed then TH chief executive officer Tan Sri Ismi Ismail to nominate him as a board member of Perdana Putra Berhad, a subsidiary, and using his position to influence TH’s board members to invest in the said company.
The alleged abuse of power, filed under Section 23-1 of the MACC Act, was said to have been committed on Aug 25, 2014, at Tabung Haji head office on Jalan Tun Abdul Razak here.
The section provides for a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the value of the gratification or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
Azeez, seen clad in purple police lock up clothing and handcuffed, pleaded not guilty and claimed trial, while asserting that the accusation “is absolutely untrue”.
The prosecution had argued that Azeez should not be allowed bail since he is being charged with a non-bailable offence, but noted that the Court still had the discretion to grant bail.
Deputy public prosecutor Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib, leading the prosecution, initially asked for bail to be set at RM1 million with additional terms.

But defence counsel Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad argued that his client’s cooperation with the authorities over the many years of investigations showed he posed no risk of fleeing, and that the bail set should not be punitive.
Sessions Court judge Azura Alwi granted Azeez bail of RM450,000 with the condition that he reports to MACC office once in three months.
Azeez is the latest person to be charged in relation to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji’s mismanagement released in July.
The report flagged 14 problematic investments, including in Putrajaya Perdana that resulted in a RM193.5 million loss.
a5161df76babd77c: WASHINGTON, Sept 9 — US President Donald Trump yesterday escalated his trade war against Canada, banning imports of alcohol and various products and raising tariffs on others, with the conflict showing no sign of abating.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stood firm, acknowledging that reducing economic ties with the United States would come at a cost but saying the benefits would outweigh the pain.

A range of Canadian products, from mattresses to motorboats and golf carts, will be subject to a 50-per cent surcharge beginning September 15, according to Trump’s executive order issued late Tuesday.
The import ban, which targets various alcoholic beverages as well as some dairy products like whey, will come into effect on September 29, according to other executive orders issued at the same time.

Canada’s retaliatory tariffs came into effect earlier yesterday, applying to C$27.6 billion (RM81.1 billion) in US imports, including steel and aluminium products and dairy goods such as cheese, in response to duties announced by Washington on August 22.
Canada has “everything we need to pivot and prosper,” Carney said in a video address.
“That pivot will come at a cost. There’s always a cost to action. But it doesn’t come close to the cost of standing still.”
‘Discriminatory treatment’
Responding to the latest Canadian levies, Trump pledged to restrict Canadian companies from securing US government contracts.

In a social media post earlier yesterday, Trump said he was directing officials “to REMOVE Canadian-origin products from GSA’s Multiple Award Schedules,” referring to a General Services Administration program for long-term contracts.
Contracts through such schedules account for more than US$50 billion (RM202 billion) a year, Trump added.
On Monday, Trump threatened to try to block sales of Canada’s Bombardier Aviation unless the Quebec-based plane maker moves manufacturing to the United States.

In response, the aerospace company pointed to its creation of tens of thousands of jobs across the United States, with direct employment in more than 20 states, including Kansas, Texas, Arizona, and California.
The two Republican senators representing Kansas said they had conveyed their concerns to the White House.

“I’m going to fight to keep Bombardier’s more than 1,200 Kansas jobs. I’ve already taken that concern inside the Oval Office,” Senator Roger Marshall posted on X, with similar comments posted by Senator Jerry Moran.
US tariffs pose a modestly negative risk to Canada’s overall economy, but analysts note that they have a sharper impact on central Canada’s manufacturing sector.
‘Lake America’

“I don’t believe in escalating the conflict. That’s not constructive,” Carney said in his video statement Tuesday. “But our tariffs are necessary to protect our workers, protect our companies, and protect our communities.
“This is about who we are as Canadians.”
Reacting to Trump’s move, Canada’s minister in charge of trade with the United States, Dominic LeBlanc, said late Tuesday that Ottawa was “assessing the latest tariff measures.”
Negotiations between the two sides broke down on August 21 after days of meetings in Washington.

At the time, Carney said US negotiators had introduced restrictions on Canadian trade deals with other countries at the eleventh hour, as well as unacceptable “threats” to the French language and “Quebec culture.” Ottawa and Washington have not resumed talks since.

On Sunday, Trump posted an illustration of himself towering over Carney as they played ice hockey, with Trump saying, “Get up, governor,” a reference to his determination to turn Canada into another US state.

Trump also signed an order in August to rename Lake Ontario, on the border with Canada, as “Lake America,” sparking fury in Canada amid a broader wave of patriotism triggered by the US president’s hostility.

Although Carney is backed by Canadian public opinion, his country remains reliant on its neighbour. Nearly 60 per cent of Canada’s imports come from the United States, and about 70 per cent of its exports go to the US market.
To help businesses and workers, Canada’s government has unveiled an aid package worth C$7.5 billion (US$5.4 billion). — AFP
e67ca8fd8a657de3: WASHINGTON: Treasury secretary Scott Bessent warned the US faces dire consequences if it loses out in the AI race with China, highlighting the angst in Washington about its rival’s tech advances.

“There is no day after tomorrow if China wins at this,” Bessent said at a Breitbart News event in Washington on Tuesday, indicating also that the US’s large defence budget would fail to protect the nation. “If they were to pull away from us on AI, then nothing else would matter.”

The comments appear aimed at some voices in the US upset that large data centre projects are getting built in their backyards. Late last month, president Donald Trump warned that a growing public backlash to the projects in the US poses an economic threat and risks giving China the upper hand in AI.
In China, many new projects are going up far from big cities in less populated regions in the north and northwest.

Bessent’s remarks also highlight worries in the US about open-weight Chinese models that are nearly as powerful as American versions at a fraction of the cost for the user. That’s happening even though the US has tried to deny China access to its most advanced tech.

Also on Tuesday, US government agencies said Alibaba Group Holding Ltd, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and other China-based AI companies “extracted billions of tokens across millions of exchanges/requests from US frontier AI models,” including variants of Anthropic PBC’s Claude, Alphabet’s Gemini and SpaceXAI’s Grok since at least late 2024.
Tokens are units of data processed by models during training and inference. They enable prediction, generation and reasoning.

The actions were potentially taken “with Chinese government awareness,” the Federal Bureau of Investigation, National Security Agency and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said in a statement.

Reuters has reported that the US and China were preparing to discuss AI safety risks in mid-September, talks that if they happened would come just before Chinese leader Xi Jinping meets Trump in Washington on Sept 24.
f45bdb75e13af666: LOS ANGELES, Sept 9 — LIV Golf, the breakaway tour that spent billions of dollars luring top players away from the PGA and triggered bitter divisions within the sport, filed yesterday for bankruptcy protection.
The filing at a New Jersey court indicates LIV, which abruptly lost its deep-pocketed Saudi investors earlier this year, intends to restructure and return in a new form.

But documents show LIV owes between US$500 million and US$1 billion (RM2 billion and RM4.06 billion) in estimated liabilities to at least 1,000 creditors, including star players like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm.

And the future of those popular players remains deeply unclear. The likes of DeChambeau are now faced with deciding whether to remain with the tour in its new guise, or leave and attempt to pursue the millions of dollars they are owed in court.
“This process gives us the structure and time to pursue a landmark transaction and begin the next chapter of LIV Golf,” said CEO Scott O’Neil, in a statement.
LIV still intends to return next year in a new form including “an innovative, player-first ownership model,” he said.
“No definitive decisions regarding the 2027 schedule or individual events are being announced at this time,” the LIV statement added.

The bankruptcy filing was widely expected, after LIV axed the majority of its staff earlier this month, and scrapped its season-ending team championship in August after losing the backing of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).
Since LIV’s launch in 2022, the Middle Eastern fund had poured an estimated US$5 billion into the tour, before abruptly pulling the plug.
The PIF will now provide a loan worth nearly US$50 million for the bankruptcy and reorganization process, the LIV statement showed.

LIV’s star players Rahm, DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson hold the largest unsecured claims against the tour, totalling more than US$5 million each in immediate past-due payments, per the bankruptcy filing.

But even those amounts do not reflect the future remaining contract values of some golfers, that can range into tens of millions of dollars each, the Financial Times reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.
Yesterday’s statement said “the Company remains in advanced discussions with” players, including on “creating an ownership structure aligning players’ interests with the League’s long-term success.”
“Players will have the opportunity to share directly in the value they help create,” said O’Neil, in an open letter to fans.
LIV did not immediately respond to AFP request for comment on the matter.
Tour officials have previously pledged that a “2.0” version of the tour will re-emerge under new investors next season, with a shorter schedule and reduced prize money.
Further details emerged for the proposals yesterday.
LIV intends to host tournaments across five continents, in locations including Australia, South Africa, Mexico, England, Hong Kong and the US.
“We intend to expand our fields to 75 players, introduce a cut, and create additional pathways for players to earn their way into LIV Golf, including Monday qualifiers,” it said.
The emphasis would remain on courting young fans, with live music, and team competitions which will “embrace national identities, building on the passion and momentum of World Cup-style competition.”
But much will depend on whether top stars including DeChambeau and Rahm remain.
Widespread reports have linked several LIV stars with potential returns to the PGA Tour and other series, though the PGA said it currently has no plans to offer LIV players a pathway back.
Five-time major winner Brooks Koepka — who did return to the PGA this year — is still listed as a creditor owed US$1.7 million on the LIV bankruptcy filing.
Yesterday’s filing confirmed LIV has partnered for the restructuring effort with British investment group BC Partners — long rumoured to be the tour’s mystery new “lead investor.”
LIV Golf is also seeking recognition of the US bankruptcy filing in England and Wales to cover its global assets, which total US$100-US$500 million. — AFP
f3dcd739554e4c45: KUALA LUMPUR: Ketua Pemuda Bersatu Hilman Idham menggesa kerajaan mempercepat pemansuhan Akta Hasutan 1948 selepas Mahkamah Majistret membebaskannya daripada pertuduhan menimbulkan kegentaran awam menerusi kenyataan di media sosial.
Adun Gombak Setia itu berkata undang-undang yang dianggap sudah lapuk perlu dimansuhkan bagi memastikan Malaysia terus bergerak ke arah sebuah negara yang lebih maju.
"Akta Hasutan antara akta yang sudah tidak lagi wajar ada dalam negara kita.

“Saya menyeru kerajaan supaya akta-akta seperti ini dimansuhkan. Akta Universiti dan Kolej Universiti 1971 (Auku) sudah dimansuhkan (diumumkan oleh Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim pada 14 Ogos). Akta Hasutan belum lagi (dimansuhkan),” katanya pada sidang media di lobi Mahkamah Kuala Lumpur.

522730a3d0104dfe: SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — Sungei Ujong Undang Dato’ Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari Meor Ngah today said a declaration purportedly signed by the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar concerning the removal of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, was invalid and could not take effect.

“Any matter concerning the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan at present must have our decree in our capacity as Imam of the Undang Yang Empat,” he said.

The statement followed a claim by another group of traditional leaders that Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had signed the proclamation at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on August 3, completing the document first issued on April 19.
The group, comprising the Undang Yang Empat, Tunku Besar Tampin and Datuk Shahbandar Sungei Ujong, called for the proclamation to be enforced immediately.

Ismail, who was sworn in as menteri besar before Tuanku Muhriz on August 2, reaffirmed his full support and loyalty to the ruler on September 6 but did not directly address whether he had signed the document.
